stories.title: Blood test reports in 1.5 minutes:AI machine installed at Gorakhpur District Women’s Hospital; over 15 tests conducted in 2 days
stories.summary: At Gorakhpur District Women’s Hospital, a new AI machine will provide reports for tests such as haemoglobin and urine in just 1–1.5 minutes. SIC Dr Anil Jha says the Sixtpal AI-100 has been installed in the pathology room, providing patients with advanced testing facilities. The machine is used to detect different types of anaemia and cancer cells. Once a sample is placed on the slide, the report is sent to the pathologist’s registered mobile number within 1–1.5 minutes. Outside tests can take 3–4 hours or up to 24 hours, while emergency reports may take around an hour. Daily monitoring Testing with the machine begins on Wednesday, with 15–20 tests conducted in two days. The results are being continuously monitored and recorded in a dedicated register. Savings of 500 to 3,000 rupees SIC informed that this test is very expensive. In outside pathology labs, this test costs from 500 to 3000 rupees. With this machine, all their money is being saved. All types of tests are being done completely free of charge. Established at a cost of approximately 38 lakhs According to information, this machine has been established at a cost of approximately 38 lakh rupees. It is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities. All its features are AI-based. This device prepares high-resolution digital images of samples. Microscopic examination to be conducted This device is automatic and will accurately complete the microscopic examination of blood and urine. With the arrival of this machine, pathologists and doctors will no longer need to spend hours examining samples under a microscope. Reports will be available in minutes Health department to receive 11 more machines SIC Dr. Anil Jha informed that this machine has been installed first at the District Women's Hospital. The trial will run for a few days. If the response is better, 11 more machines will soon be provided to the health department, which will be installed at various health centers. DM reviewed DM Deepak Meena visited the Pathology department located in the MCH wing and took stock of the machine's work capacity and quality. He spoke with the trainer who accompanied the machine and the pathologists undergoing training, gathering information about the machine's features and operation. The DM instructed the pathologists to thoroughly understand the working of this AI-based state-of-the-art machine so that patients can receive better testing facilities.

stories.title: Daughter kills father with lover:They attacked his neck and chest with sickle; he had caught them in a compromising position
stories.summary: In Basti, a 17-year-old girl, along with her 21-year-old lover, murdered her father. The father had seen them in an objectionable state in the field. He scolded his daughter and opposed the lover. During this, he had an argument and a scuffle with the lover. After this, the daughter and the lover together attacked the father's neck, chest, and face multiple times with a sickle. According to the police, after the murder, the body was thrown into the bushes along the canal. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon around 1 PM in the Chhawani police station area, about 35 kilometers from the district headquarters. The deceased has been identified as Krishna (50) from Ramwapur village. See pictures Now know the full story Krishna (50), a resident of Ramwapur village, used to support his family by working as a labourer. He has two daughters. The elder daughter is married, while the 17-year-old daughter lived with him. Her mother died shortly after her birth. Krishna's brother, Kashiram, stated that his niece left home around 9 AM on Friday to graze cattle. When she did not return home by around 12 PM, Krishna went out to look for her. Saw daughter with her lover Krishna reached the fields while searching for his daughter. There, he saw her in an objectionable state with Lakshman (21), a resident of Babhrauli village. He scolded his daughter and also confronted the young man. During this, a scuffle broke out between Krishna and Lakshman. After that, the daughter and Lakshman together attacked Krishna with a sickle. Both inflicted several blows on Krishna's neck, chest, and face. After the murder, the body was taken and thrown into the bushes near the canal. According to villagers, Krishna's daughter had been in a love affair with Lakshman for about a year. Lakshman works in shuttering. Villagers say that the girl had gone to meet Lakshman on the pretext of grazing cattle and had also taken a sickle with her for cutting grass. Secret revealed during questioning of daughter When Krishna did not return home late in the evening, his family became worried. They asked his daughter about her father, but she denied any knowledge. Krishna's mobile phone was also at home. When the family became suspicious, they questioned the daughter strictly. She then revealed that her father had been murdered. She said that the body was lying near the canal in Babhrauli village, about 500 meters from the village. Hearing this, family members and villagers reached the spot. Krishna's body was found lying amidst bushes on the canal bank. There were marks of sickle blows on his neck, chest, and face. Upon receiving information, SO Jeevan Tripathi arrived at the spot with his force. The police sent the body for post-mortem. SO said FIR registered and questioning is underway SO Jeevan Tripathi said: “A case has been registered in the matter. The minor girl and her lover have been taken into custody and are being questioned. The matter is being investigated.”

stories.title: 3 youths die from toxic gas in UP's Chandauli:They entered well to remove submersible pump; one in critical condition
stories.summary: Four people were exposed to toxic gas while entering a closed well to retrieve a submersible pump in Chandauli on Saturday. Three of them died, while the fourth remains in critical condition. With the help of local residents and police, all four were pulled out of the well and taken to hospital. Doctors declared three of them dead, while the fourth is undergoing treatment and remains in serious condition. The incident occurred at around 2.30 pm in Kidahira village under Shahabganj police station. A faulty submersible pump was stuck inside a well in Kidahira village and efforts were underway to retrieve it. During the operation, four people entered the well one after another. They were overcome by toxic gas inside the well and collapsed unconscious. When there was no movement from inside and the people outside received no response despite calling out, panic spread among the villagers.

stories.title: Akhilesh says BJP means ‘Bhag Jao Pakistan’:SP chief adds, 'Dynastic politics has benefits too-5 MPs in his family, keeping SP united'
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav explained on Saturday why the party has remained intact despite several political parties splitting across the country. He said, “Have you ever wondered why the SP did not break? Because there are five MPs from the same family. There are also several Muslim MPs and some committed socialist MPs. Sometimes, dynastic politics can also have its advantages.” Speaking at a press conference at the SP office, Akhilesh hit back at CM Yogi Adityanath’s remarks on PDA. He said, They are saying that the ‘P’ in PDA stands for Pakistan. So I would say BJP means ‘Bhag Jao Pakistan’ (Run Away to Pakistan). The more the suffering increases, the stronger PDA will become. PDA also means ‘Prem, Daya, Apnapan’ (Love, Compassion and Belongingness). Akhilesh added, “The more we socialists connect people through love, compassion and belongingness, the stronger the SP will become. It will form a historic government in the future.” Actually, CM Yogi had said on Friday, “These are people who change colors like chameleons. First, they defined ‘P’ as ‘Pichhda’ (Backward), then changed it to ‘Pandit’. One day, they may define ‘P’ as ‘Pakistan’ too.”

stories.title: Objectionable videos of female students recorded in library:Owner’s son arrested for filming through hole in washroom wall, landlord's son arrested
stories.summary: Case of allegedly recording objectionable videos of female students in the washroom of a digital library has come to light in Bhadohi. The accused, the son of the building owner, allegedly made a hole in the washroom wall and secretly recorded the students on his mobile phone. Police said, "He had allegedly been recording the videos for around two months. The students became suspicious and informed the library operator on Thursday. They checked the accused’s mobile phone and allegedly found 12 videos. The matter was subsequently reported to the police. Police questioned the accused strictly, after which he confessed and began apologizing, saying he would not repeat the mistake. The incident took place in the Gopiganj police station area, around 12 km from the district headquarters. His mobile phone has been seized. Police are investigating how many videos he recorded, whether he shared any of them and whether any videos were deleted. Digital library had been operating for 2 years Library named New Digital operates on the first floor of a two storey building in Lalannagar and has been running for around two years under the management of Bharthari Bind. A total of 28 students, 12 girls and 16 boys study there while preparing for online examinations. The building is owned by Lal Bahadur Gupta. The library occupies the first floor, while his son Ravi Gupta runs a grocery shop on the ground floor. Ravi also has a room next to the library, which he used for storing goods. The wall of the girls’ washroom is adjacent to this room. Recorded videos through a hole drilled in the wall Library operator Bharthari Bind said, “The accused had made a hole in the wall of the girls’ washroom. Whenever the students went to the washroom, he would place his mobile phone in the hole and secretly record videos. The girls had suspected Ravi several times earlier, but no one had filed a complaint." She continued, "On Thursday, when the library’s internet connection developed a problem, the students came outside. During this time, Ravi was repeatedly going in and out of his room, which again raised the girls’ suspicions. The students complained to me about this. When Ravi realized that we suspected him, he left his mobile phone behind and fled.” Videos of female students found on his phone The library operator said, “When Ravi returned, I and the students went to his room and asked him to unlock his mobile phone. During the search, videos of female students were found on the phone. We then informed the police about the matter." She added, "PRB personnel took Ravi into custody and brought him to the police station. I filed a written complaint against him. Parents of several female students also reached the police station and demanded strict action against the accused. I have now shut down the library.” Suspected of recording videos for 2 months According to police, one video found in the mobile is 56 days old. According to police, the accused has admitted to making videos and kept apologizing continuously during interrogation. Library operator Bharthari Bind said, "He had been running the library in the rented building for nearly one and a half years. After students complained, he noticed a hole in the washroom wall. His family lives in the village Ravi Gupta is the fifth of six brothers. Three of his brothers work in Mumbai, while another brother lives there and is preparing for exams. Ravi’s grocery shop is located on the main road, while the family home is inside the village. His parents and younger brother live in the village. Ravi’s wife and two children also stay there with his parents. Station in-charge said, ‘Mobile is being examined’ Station in-charge Sachchidanand Pandey stated, One video found on the mobile phone was 56 days old, suggesting that the accused may have been recording videos for nearly two months. PRB police took the accused youth into custody and brought him to the station. When his mobile was examined, obscene videos were found in it. A case has been registered and the accused has been sent to jail.

stories.title: Plane’s tail hits ground during landing:Pilot lands on second attempt in Gorakhpur; 178 people were on board IndiGo flight
stories.summary: A major aviation incident was narrowly avoided at Gorakhpur Airport on 19 August when the rear section of an IndiGo aircraft carrying 178 people, including crew members, struck the runway during landing. The pilot immediately initiated a go-around and took the aircraft back into the air. After receiving clearance from Air Traffic Control (ATC), the flight landed safely a short while later. The Delhi-Gorakhpur flight, 6E 2381, was carrying 178 passengers and crew members. During a routine post-landing inspection, scratches were found near the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) at the rear of the aircraft. The aircraft has been temporarily taken out of service and is undergoing technical inspection and repairs. Airport authorities said it will be cleared for operations only after receiving the required technical approval. An IndiGo spokesperson said, The decision to initiate the go-around was taken purely as a safety precaution. The safety of passengers, crew and the flight remains our highest priority. IndiGo flight delayed by over five hours after aircraft incident The incident also affected IndiGo flight 6E-5013, scheduled to operate from Gorakhpur to Delhi. The flight departed around 5 hours and 30 minutes behind schedule, leaving passengers waiting at the airport and disrupting some connecting flights and other planned engagements. IndiGo arranged an alternative aircraft, VT-IBC, to operate the service. Passengers were provided breakfast and meals during the delay, while those needing to travel urgently were offered alternative flight options. Other passengers were provided refunds as per the applicable rules.

stories.title: NSUI leaders back Gen Z in Lucknow:Plan to gherao Raj Bhavan, demand Amit Shah’s resignation; police deployed without nameplates
stories.summary: In Lucknow, NSUI workers came out on the streets on Saturday in support of Gen-Z. Demanding the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, they set out to gherao the Raj Bhavan. During this, many of the deployed policemen did not wear nameplates. The plan was to gherao the Raj Bhavan by taking out a march of more than 2 km from Parivartan Chowk to the Assembly. As soon as the protesting workers reached near Babu KD Singh Stadium, 300 metres from Parivartan Sthal, the police stopped them there. From there, each worker was picked up and put into vehicles and sent to Eco Garden. The protesting NSUI workers said that the police action in the Gen-Z students' movement at Jantar Mantar had spread outrage. Deepak Shivhare, UP State President of Youth Congress (NSUI), was leading these protesting workers. Congress UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, National Secretary Jagdish Chandra Jangid, and Abdul Hannan also participated in the protest. MP Rakesh Rathore and former MLC Deepak Singh, along with many senior leaders, also joined. All were sent to Eco Garden by the police. About an hour and a half before this protest by the Youth Congress, at 11:30 AM, a heavy police force was deployed at the Parivartan Sthal. Former MLC Deepak Singh said: “Our movement will not stop until Home Minister Amit Shah resigns. If the police force deployed to stop us had put in this much effort to prevent paper leaks, there would have been no protests.”

stories.title: Boyfriend travels 1,000km to Ludhiana to meet girlfriend:Elopes with her promising marriage, police trap him; family alleges rape
stories.summary: Teenage boy allegedly traveled around 1,000 km to Ludhiana to meet his 15 year old minor girlfriend. He allegedly called her out of her house and took her away after promising to marry her. When the family discovered that the girl was missing, they began searching for her but could not find any trace of her for nearly two weeks. They then provided the accused’s mobile number to the police. After tracing the number, police found that the two were in the Focal Point area. The family reached the location and found the minor wandering on the street. Shortly afterward, the accused also arrived at the spot. The family caught him and handed him over to the police. The family has alleged, “She might have been raped. Police said she will undergo a medical examination to determine whether she was sexually assaulted. Her age is reported to be 15, while the accused told police that he was also 15 years old. Police are verifying his age.” Know the full story of his journey from UP to Ludhiana to eloping with his girlfriend Minor stayed with him for 14 days, family suspects rape Meanwhile, the family said, “She stayed with the accused for about 14 days. The family has expressed suspicion of rape during this period. She has not yet given clear information about the incident.” The police will now conduct her medical examination. Only based on the medical report and investigation will it become clear whether she was raped or not. Police told, ‘Girl will undergo medical examination’ According to investigating officer Raj Gopal, the accused has been arrested and an FIR has been registered against him. Currently, action has been taken under sections related to kidnapping and keeping a minor in confinement. The minor's medical examination is being conducted. If rape is confirmed in the medical examination and investigation, then relevant sections will be added to the FIR.

stories.title: ‘Forced us to dance to Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai’:Meerut SSP acts on SP leader’s allegation; 8 cops sent to lines
stories.summary: Eight policemen, including an inspector, were sent to line duty after allegations of assaulting SP leaders.New SSP BBGTS Murthy took the action soon after assuming charge in Meerut. On Friday, SP leaders Dr. Digvijay Bhati and Mohit Jatav held a press conference. Digvijay Bhati arrived with a bandage over his injured eye and broke down while showing his wounds. He said, “We had no idea that the SSP harbored such hatred toward us. He beat us and repeatedly kicked us with his boots. Both of us suffered internal injuries, and one of my eyes became swollen.” He further alleged, “He kept beating us until we lost consciousness. After this, Inspector Civil Lines Akhilesh Gaud was handed over to us. He took us to the SOG office at Police Lines, where we were subjected to brutality. Whenever we lost consciousness, they brought us back to our senses and continued beating us.” He stated, The policemen played a song on mobile - 'Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai...' They repeatedly asked us to dance to this song. We couldn't even stand, yet we were being made to dance. Everyone was laughing at us. We were folding our hands (pleading), but no one showed mercy. Meerut Police has dismissed the allegations as baseless, saying both men are history sheeters and that their injuries were caused by falling from a scooter. When Dainik Bhaskar asked Inspector Akhilesh about the allegations, he said, “I reached the spot later. I only followed the orders given to me by the SSP.” As the matter escalated, Meerut ADG Bhanu Bhaskar assigned Saharanpur DIG Abhishek Singh to investigate the case. On Thursday night, the state government transferred nine IPS officers, including SSP Avinash Pandey, who was removed from the post and attached to the Lucknow Police Headquarters. See 2 pictures, Read SP Leader Dr. Digvijay Bhati’s allegations Bharatiya Kisan Union (BR Ambedkar) President Dr. Digvijay Bhati stated that on 19 August, I and our district president Mohit went to meet SSP Avinash Pandey. The police had sent 8-10 of us to jail in connection with the Lalita Gautam murder case protest demonstration. We had done nothing wrong nor were we involved in the protest. That's why we went to meet the Captain Sahab to present our case. When we met the SSP, he got furious. Using abusive language, he started saying, "Wearing a 40 rupee kurta-pajama, you become a leader, you'll confront me?" He added, “When we protested against the abusive language, the SSP dragged us into his chamber and beat us with kicks, punches, and shoes. After this, he told Civil Lines in-charge Akhilesh Gaud to see how much hospitality you can show. Then he took us to the SOG (Special Operations Group) office. In a closed room, they tied our hands and feet and beat us with sticks. We were released at 2 AM when Atul Pradhan arrived. A condition was imposed that if the matter came to the media, we would be dealt with even worse.” “SSP had already planned our encounter” Digvijay Bhati said while crying, “We were not involved in the 8 July protest, yet we were targeted. We came forward to get justice for a poor family. If this keeps happening, no one will come forward to help anyone in need.” Mohit Jatav said, “He is a leader of his community. Before going to the office, he had a phone conversation with the police officer. The behavior on the phone was completely different from the behavior in person. The SSP had already planned our encounter. He had told the policemen to shoot one bullet at me and then carry out the encounter. I will handle everything.” 10 more cases against Digvijay in Meerut-Amroha, 7 against Mohit According to police, Digvijay Singh Bhati, son of Raghuraj Singh and a resident of Chamarwa in Sambhal, and Mohit Jatav, son of Suresh Singh and a resident of Kinanagar in Meerut, already have several cases registered against them. Both are listed as history-sheeters at their respective police stations. Police said Digvijay has five cases each registered in Meerut and Amroha, while Mohit has seven cases registered in Meerut.

stories.title: Man kills wife and daughter for not having son:Stabs them in Ghaziabad; younger daughter escapes and saves her life
stories.summary: Father (45 year old) allegedly murdered his wife (35 year old) and daughter (15 year old) by stabbing them with a knife in Ghaziabad, reportedly because they had not had a son. When his younger daughter tried to save them, he allegedly attacked her as well. She somehow escaped and ran out of the house screaming for help. Hearing her cries, neighbors reached the spot, overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police. The incident took place around midnight on Friday in Lokpriya Vihar Colony under the Khoda police station area. The accused has been identified as Raja Ansari (45), a native of Araria, Bihar. He works as a clerk at Khoda Mandi and lives with his family in a rented house. Police have taken the accused into custody and sent the bodies of his wife, Tabassum (35), and daughter, Sana (15), for post-mortem. His injured 14 year old daughter has been admitted to a hospital. Now, know what happened… Raja Ansari’s younger daughter said, “Fight broke out between my parents late Friday night over an issue, my father often argued with my mother over not having a son, and the both of them were fighting over the same issue that night." During the argument, the father allegedly went to the kitchen, returned with a knife and repeatedly attacked his wife. When the elder daughter tried to save her mother, he allegedly attacked her as well., both fell to the floor covered in blood. The accused then allegedly chased his younger daughter with the knife. She ran out of the house screaming and told the neighbors, “Father has stabbed mother and sister with a knife.” The neighbors then caught the accused and informed the police. Police called a forensic team to the scene and collected evidence. The accused has been taken into custody and is being interrogated. Neighbors told, “He took drugs, often fought with wife” According to neighbors, Raja takes drugs and has an angry temperament. They also claim, “He often fought with his wife over not having a son.” The neighbors tried to make him understand several times, but he did not listen. Had little interaction with neighbors According to neighbor Babu Khan, Raja's family members rarely left the house and had minimal interaction with people. On Friday night around 12 o'clock, when screams and cries were heard from Raja's house, neighbors rushed there. When they looked inside, Raja's wife and daughter were lying drenched in blood. ACP, “Motive behind the murder is being investigated…”

stories.title: Mayawati calls Akhilesh arrogant, demands apology to Jayant:Calls ‘turning a nobody into a somebody’ remark shameful; says SP exploited Brahmins
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati has hit out at Akhilesh Yadav over his remark, “turned four annas into a rupee.” Calling the SP chief arrogant, she said, “The statement reflects his 'indecent conduct'.” She alleged, “Akhilesh had insulted the family of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh.” Mayawati said, “Akhilesh should immediately apologize not only to RLD leader Jayant Chaudhary but also to the entire Jat community, the Samajwadi Party has consistently ‘oppressed’ Brahmins.” Mayawati made these remarks in a post on X on Saturday morning, Due to SP's arrogant attitude, BSP's alliance with Mulayam Singh Yadav broke down quickly in 1993. After this, on June 2, 1995, a conspiracy was hatched to kill me. The infamous Lucknow State Guest House incident happened against me. Mayawati said, “Akhilesh Yadav had also assured me that he would not repeat the mistakes made by his father in the past. Trusting this assurance, the SP and BSP joined hands for the Lok Sabha elections. However, the election results did not meet expectations.” Soon after, the alliance between the two parties fell apart. Mayawati tole, “This happened because of the SP’s “arrogant and selfish” attitude.” Read Mayawati’s 3 key points 1. SP changes colors like a chameleon for its own benefit Mayawati said, “The Samajwadi Party knows how to use alliances only for its own political benefit. Once its purpose is served, the party “changes colors like a chameleon” and later uses inappropriate language against its former allies, the SP’s long-standing attitude and urged people from all communities to remain cautious of its 'narrow and casteist politics'.” 2. Akhilesh gives different meanings to ‘P’ in PDA for political gain Mayawati alleged, “Akhilesh Yadav interprets the “P” in his PDA formula differently according to his political interests. At times, he links it to backward classes, while at other times he associates it with the interests of Pandits.” She further alleged, “Apart from its own caste among the backward classes, the SP has not worked in the interests of other OBCs, minorities and, particularly, the Brahmin community.” 3. It was difficult for women to step out during SP rule Mayawati alleged, “During previous SP governments, Dalits, backward classes, minorities and especially the Brahmin community were exploited and oppressed, with no meaningful steps taken for their welfare. Goons, criminals, mafias and anarchic elements benefited under SP rule, while law and order remained poor, it was difficult for women and girls to step out of their homes during that period." Mayawati appealed to people from all sections of society not to allow the SP to return to power in the upcoming Assembly elections, calling it a matter of public interest. She said, “The BSP would never compromise on the principles of self-respect and dignity championed by Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar, the party would remain committed to its Ambedkarite ideology and the principle of “Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay” welfare and happiness for all.” Jayant had counterattacked on Akhilesh's statement Now, read about the guest house incident mentioned by BSP supremo

stories.summary: On Friday, a joint team of Railway Administration, Traffic Police, and Municipal Corporation conducted an anti-encroachment drive around Gorakhpur Railway Station. During this campaign, which was carried out on both outer sides of the station and in surrounding areas, illegally placed handcarts, vendors, and other encroachments on the road and station pathways were removed. Additionally, challans were issued for unauthorised parked vehicles. Passengers facing problems due to traffic jams Station Director Ratandeep Gupta stated that for the past several days, continuous complaints of traffic jams were being received from around Gorakhpur Railway Station. A large number of unauthorised carts and vendors were standing outside the station. Additionally, many people used to park their two-wheelers unauthorizedly on the roadside. Because of this, the road around the station would narrow, and traffic was getting affected. The biggest problem was being faced by passengers reaching the station to catch trains. Many passengers had complained that they feared missing their train due to getting stuck in traffic. Railways, municipal corporation, and traffic police took joint action A joint campaign was launched to improve passenger convenience and traffic management around the station. The campaign was led by Station Director Gorakhpur Ratandeep Gupta, Additional Municipal Commissioner Atul Kumar, and SP Traffic Amit Kumar Srivastava. During this time, employees from various departments of the Municipal Corporation, Railway Protection Force (RPF), and the commercial department team of the Railways were also present at the spot. The joint team inspected the roads around the station and the entry-exit routes, taking action to remove encroachments. Challans issued for unauthorised vehicles During the campaign, action was taken against several two-wheelers parked unauthorizedly on the road around the station. Challans were issued for such vehicles, and drivers were warned not to park vehicles illegally on the road. Along with this, unauthorized stalls and other temporary encroachments set up on the road and the station's path were also removed. Officials clarified that action would be taken against those who encroach again around the station. Passengers should not face difficulty in catching trains Officials stated that the main objective of the campaign is to provide passengers with a clean and smooth path to reach the station. If there is no traffic congestion around the station, passengers will be able to reach the station on time, and the problem of missing trains will also be reduced. Officials said that unauthorised carts, vendors, and vehicles will not be allowed to park on the road to keep the traffic system smooth outside the station. Campaign will continue further Railway administration, municipal corporation, and traffic police clarified that this action will not be limited to just one day. Joint anti-encroachment campaigns will be conducted from time to time to ensure passenger convenience and unobstructed access to the station. Officials say that along with improving the traffic system around the station, priority is being given to the safety and convenience of passengers, so that they do not face any problems while coming to and going from the station and can catch their trains on time.

stories.title: ‘He killed my daughter for refusing to marry him’:Varanasi M.Sc student’s father says, ‘He wanted property, not love; blackmailed her extensively’
stories.summary: If my Shreya had ever been in trouble, she would definitely have called us. We started calling her from 2:30 pm that day, but she did not answer even once. After that, my daughter never came back. She was murdered. My daughter deserves justice. Shreya's mother breaks down and faints while recounting the incident in Varanasi. She still remembers the morning when her 22-year-old daughter, M.Sc student Shreya Upadhyay, leaves home for college as usual. However, Shreya never returns. Her body is later found in the bathroom of her friend Vivek Chaubey's rented room, around 5 km from her home. The bathroom door is reportedly locked from the outside. After regaining consciousness, Shreya's mother alleges that Vivek repeatedly blackmails her daughter. Shreya's father, in tears, alleges that Vivek does not love his only daughter but has his eyes on the family's property. He says Shreya does not want to marry Vivek, so the family arranges her marriage elsewhere. ‘He pressured her to marry him’ According to Shreya's family, Vivek continues pressuring her to marry him and also threatens her mother. The family alleges that Vivek takes Shreya to his room while she is on her way to college and kills her. Shreya's body is found at around 1:30 pm on August 20 (Thursday) in the bathroom of Vivek's rented room. To understand the family's grief and learn the full sequence of events, the Dainik Bhaskar team visits Rajatalab Marui-Jamuni village, around 22 km from Varanasi city, and speaks to Shreya's family members. ‘Daughter refused to marry vivek’ Shreya's mother, Rita Upadhyay, says people are spreading rumours that her daughter ran away from home. She says, That is not true. She went to college as she did every day. My daughter was not at fault. If she had done something wrong, perhaps she would still be alive today. Shreya's father, Sunil Upadhyay, says Vivek proposes marriage around one-and-a-half years ago, but the family does not agree. When he asks Shreya, she also refuses. My daughter tells me, ‘Dad, I will not marry him. Sunil says the family explains the situation to Vivek and his relatives. Their neighbours, who are also Vivek's relatives, assure the family that he will not trouble Shreya anymore. Vivek threatened, ‘I will also see how the wedding takes place’ Father Sunil Upadhyay said, Vivek must have been counselled by his relatives. For some time he was fine, but after some time he started coming and going again. He kept talking about marrying Shreya. We fixed Shreya's wedding in a nearby village. The engagement took place and the wedding date was set for February 2027.After this, Vivek became aggressive. He had threatened Shreya's mother, saying, ‘I will see how the wedding happens.’ Now Vivek has killed my daughter. Shreya's aunt said that Vivek had already threatened to kill Shreya's father. Vivek just wanted to marry Shreya, but Shreya was silent due to fear and pressure. Cousin asked police to break the lock, but they refused Shreya's cousin Anshuman Upadhyay alleges that Vivek escapes due to police negligence. He says that when Shreya does not return home by the evening of August 18, he goes to the police station and asks the police to trace her phone. According to Anshuman, the phone's location is traced to the Bachhaw area, where Vivek has a rented room. He says, I go there myself after getting the location, but find nothing. I inform the police, after which the station in-charge and other policemen reach the spot. The room is locked. We tell the police that Shreya's phone location is showing this place and ask them to break the lock, check inside and recover the phone. But the police refuse. Police say both are adults The family alleges that the police do not break open the lock, saying they do not have the authority to do so. The police also tell them that both Shreya and Vivek are adults and may have gone somewhere together. Family members then question people living nearby and learn that Shreya has left the area. The police team subsequently leaves the spot. Anshuman says, If the police had broken the door that night, we would have known what had happened to Shreya. Even if something had happened to her, the accused would not have had enough time to escape. We could have caught him immediately. Shreya's body found after searching Family members said that we continued to search for Shreya the next day as well. We kept gathering information about Vivek and reaching his potential hideouts. During this time, the family reached Vivek's relatives' place. His bag was found there, which contained the key to his rented room. We took the key and went back to the same room in Bachhaw, which we had previously reached with the police. The mother hoped that perhaps they would find some clue about her daughter. But, as soon as the door was opened, a strong foul smell emanated from inside. The family went inside and looked in the bathroom, where Shreya's decomposed body was found. How Vivek knew Shreya?

stories.title: Pay bribe, get Ram Lalla darshan in Ayodhya:Pay more and cop will accompany you, even arrange a reel; full deal exposed in sting
stories.summary: "You will be able to have darshan at Ram Mandir. We will get the protocol issued from the Magistrate's office, then the Sub-Inspector himself will take you and arrange the darshan." This is the statement of Shubham Dubey, a tout who arranges darshan outside the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. He is part of a gang that arranges darshan for money. The charge is ₹7,300. In reality, there is no fee for darshan at Ram Mandir. Even after the revelation of theft of offerings at Ram Mandir, Champat Rai might have been removed from the temple's management, but the system has not improved. Here, some influential people are still running a darshan nexus. For money, these people are also getting photos and reels made in the restricted area of the temple. This is charged separately. Dainik Bhaskar conducted an investigation into this. Read the full revelation In our investigation, 3 ways of arranging darshan for money at Ayodhya's Ram Mandir came to light, which are as follows- 1- VVIP Protocol in the name of Minister-Officer: Brokers take money in the name of officers-ministers and arrange darshan. This includes police personnel and employees stationed at the VIP gate, who are running a darshan nexus in collusion with brokers. 2- With Mahants-Priests: In this, after taking money, mahants-priests themselves accompany and arrange darshan. Hotel owners provide them with customers. 3- Passes even when slots are full: In this, entry passes are being sold for money even when slot bookings on the website are full. This involves collusion between temple employees and brokers. We contacted broker Shubham Dubey outside the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. Shubham made a deal to arrange darshan under VVIP protocol. Darshan Nexus-1 Reporter : Will VVIP darshan be possible? Shubham : Yes, we will arrange it. Someone will go with you and facilitate the darshan. Reporter : At what time will you arrange the darshan? Shubham : We can arrange the darshan right now. We will get a wireless message from the Magistrate's office, and VVIP entry will be arranged. Then you can show your Aadhaar card and go straight inside. Reporter : Who will accompany us? Shubham : The Daroga (Sub-Inspector) will go with you and arrange your darshan. If the police accompany you, the darshan will be excellent. You all come at 4 PM. Reporter : There won't be any problem, right? Shubham: No problem. With the pass, you will go in the VIP line, but the Sub-Inspector will take you to VVIP. Your protocol will arrive via wireless from the Magistrate's office. Your VVIP darshan will be guaranteed. Sub-Inspector facilitated darshan for ₹7,300, made a reel in a restricted area Shubham introduced us to another tout, Vimal Mishra. He took ₹7,300 from us and took us to the gate. Here, he introduced us to Sub-Inspector Rajesh Kumar. Then, after depositing mobile, wallet, and other belongings in the gate's locker, Vimal and Sub-Inspector Rajesh took us for darshan. Photo-video is prohibited in the temple premises, but in the presence of the Sub-Inspector himself, tout Vimal took our photos and also made a reel. Now we reached Hanumangarhi to have darshan at Ram Mandir through priests. Here we met hotelier Manoj. He introduced us to Arun Pandey, who was selling prasad. Arun called priest Pawandas. Pawandas made a deal to take us to Ram Mandir for darshan. Darshan Nexus-2 Reporter: Maharaj ji, will you arrange the darshan? Pawandas: Yes, we will arrange it. Reporter: How much will it cost? Pawandas: I told you, it will cost ₹1,200. Reporter: No, please reduce it a bit. Okay, take ₹1,000. Pawandas: Alright, fine. After this, priest Pawandas took us to the VIP gate of the Ram Mandir. Here, he submitted photocopies of our Aadhar cards. Then, he took us along and arranged VIP darshan of Ramlala and Ram Darbar. Despite slot booking being full, can a darshan pass be made by paying money? To find this out, we met broker Mohandas. He has a nexus with the Ram Mandir staff. He arranged for the darshan pass and sent it through his brother Ganesh. Darshan Nexus-3 Ganesh : Your passes have been made. Reporter : Give us the passes. Ganesh : What will you do with the passes? You're concerned with VIP darshan, aren't you? VIP darshan will happen. Reporter : What did we pay you for? We need the passes? Ganesh: Okay, wait, we are getting them for you. (Then Ganesh called someone and got the passes. He said) See, your passes are ready. You can take a photo of this. (We took photos of the passes that came on Ganesh's phone) Ganesh: When I've given my word, it won't be wrong. Look, check your name and Aadhaar number on the pass, it's correct, isn't it? SSP said, ‘Action will be taken against those who charge money for darshan’ Ayodhya SSP Dr. Gaurav Grover said, ‘Normal and easy darshan at Ram Mandir are completely free. For some saints, seers, or specific individuals in Ayodhya, proper passes are issued for easy/VIP darshan. The police have no role in this.’

stories.title: Boy starts barking after dog bite in Mirzapur:Doctor advises keeping him in a dark room; recovers in 22 days, first such case in UP
stories.summary: On March 16, a video of a 15-year-old boy from Mirzapur surfaces in which he is seen barking like a dog. Saliva continuously drips from his mouth, and he is unable to drink water. The boy, Karan, develops these symptoms after being bitten by a dog in December. He does not receive anti-rabies injections at the time. The doctor tells the family, ‘Lock him in a dungeon; he will die in three to four days.’ Hearing this, Karan's disabled father loses hope. However, four months after the incident, Karan is now completely healthy and attending school. His recovery is being described as the first reported case in Uttar Pradesh of a patient surviving after reaching the final stage of rabies. Here is the complete sequence of events. How Karan was bitten by a dog, what negligence occurred Karan says, On December 8, 2025, my maternal uncle Kanhaiya Lal passed away. His Terahvin (13th-day ritual) was on December 20. I had gone to my uncle's house in Harhua, Varanasi. Anil Kumar's house is in their neighborhood. He is also my maternal uncle by relation. He has a native breed dog. A 5-6 year old child was feeding something to the dog. When I pulled the child towards me, the dog bit my hand. Perhaps it thought I was hitting the child. Karan further said, People took me to the doctor. There, I got a tetanus injection. Then I came home with my father. I knew about rabies, so I also went to the hospital to get its injection. But it was very crowded there. A hospital employee claimed that if I had already received a tetanus injection, there was no need for a rabies injection. Believing him, I came home. Suddenly felt dizzy, fell down, and started barking Karan's father, Bhaiyalal, says his son shows no signs of rabies for around four months. The family is poor, and Bhaiyalal has suffered a paralysis attack. To support the family, Karan sometimes works as a labourer. On the evening of March 13, Karan returns from work and suddenly falls outside the house. The family picks him up and gives him medicine, after which he appears fine. However, the next morning, he falls again and starts barking. He cannot speak when asked anything, leaving his family frightened. Bhaiyalal says Karan's condition initially makes the family suspect a supernatural problem. They take him to the Ram-Janaki temple in Kachhwa Bazaar, where prayers continue for some time. As Karan's condition worsens, they take him to a nearby hospital. The doctor says he cannot be treated there, so the family takes him to Kachhwa Christian Hospital, where he is admitted briefly before being referred to Mirzapur District Hospital. At Mirzapur District Hospital, Karan receives one or two injections, but doctors say he will not recover there and advise the family to take him to Varanasi. By then, it is night, so Bhaiyalal takes Karan home. He continues barking throughout the night. The next day, the family manages to arrange an ambulance to take him to Varanasi. BHU doctors say, ‘Lock him in a dark room’ Karan is still barking when he reaches BHU and cannot speak, although he understands everything. He recalls doctors telling the family that he will not survive and advising them to lock him alone in a dark room, keep everyone away from him and not let anyone touch him. They say he will die within three to four days. Doctors give this advice because Karan is trying to bite people and is considered to be in the final stage of rabies. Bhaiyalal says the family's courage breaks after hearing this. They tell doctors that even if Karan cannot survive, they want to take him home. Doctors then suggest taking him to Kapil Chaura Hospital for another opinion. At Kapil Chaura Hospital, two doctors sprinkle a little water on Karan, causing him to tremble. They offer him water, but he cannot drink it. The doctors also lose hope and the family then takes him to Rama Center Hospital, where doctors again say there is no hope of survival and advise them to take him away. Karan's recovery story Bhaialal says, 'When we gave up after showing him to everyone in Varanasi, I called my in-laws. My brother-in-law's son said to bring him to Harhua (a town in Varanasi) to us. There was a relative named Suman, who was at the Harhua Primary Health Center but had retired. He saw Karan and then got him a rabies vaccine the next morning. Three days later, he got another vaccine. Bhaialal says, After a week, the third vaccine was administered. Two more vaccines were given in the next two weeks. A total of 5 rabies vaccines were given in about 22 days. Karan started recovering. We brought him home. After a month, he started having problems again. We called the doctor there, and they called him back and gave two more vaccines at 1-week intervals. Now Karan is perfectly fine. When Karan's health deteriorated, 2 videos went viral- Karan studies in class 9 We asked if anything changed after the dog incident? Karan says that it's still the same as before. He enjoys studying. His friends also play with him. Teachers also don't discriminate in any way. Everyone sits together. Karan's house is about 15 kilometers away from Mirzapur district headquarters, near Kachhwa market. Karan has 2 elder brothers and one sister. His mother passed away about 10 years ago. Four years ago, his father Bhaiyalal also suffered a paralysis attack. Now he stays at home. How did he recover from rabies? Rabies is an incurable disease. So how did he recover? We understood this from the doctor who treated Karan- 7 ignjections given Dr Santosh Kumar, Superintendent of Harhua Primary Health Centre in Varanasi, says Karan arrives with hydrophobia and barking. He is given an anti-rabies injection, and within 24 hours, his aggression appears to decrease. He says the family is advised to complete the full course. Normally, five anti-rabies doses are given, starting from the day of the dog bite. Although Karan receives treatment late, he completes five doses over 22 days, followed by two additional doses. He is now reportedly fine. Doctor explains why Karan may have survived Dr Devendra Pratap Patel of Pratapgarh District Hospital explains that the location of the dog bite and timing of symptoms can affect how quickly rabies progresses. Karan is bitten on the hand, which is farther from the brain, so the infection may take longer to produce symptoms. A bite on the neck or chest could allow the virus to reach the brain more quickly, making survival much more difficult. Another factor is that the dog is reportedly a pet and may have received an anti-rabies vaccination. This could possibly explain why Karan develops symptoms only after four months. How did the vaccine help after symptoms appeared? Dr Patel says it is possible that the infection has not completely overwhelmed Karan. He also raises the possibility that reading or hearing about rabies may have had a psychological effect on the child after he remembered the dog bite and began barking. He says doctors may have considered the barking as the basis for their assessment. However, he describes the case as unique and says detailed study could help clarify several aspects. How does the rabies vaccine work? Dr Patel explains that a vaccine acts as an antigen. After entering the body, it triggers the production of antibodies against the rabies virus, which takes around 3–4 days. The rabies virus gradually travels towards the brain through the nerves, and the later symptoms are linked to its effect on the brain.

stories.title: Is Champat hinting at scam in Ram Temple construction?:Letter appears to suggest so; Nripendra hasn’t met Champat since donation theft
stories.summary: The ‘internal strife’ that began after the alleged theft of offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple has now surfaced openly. After indications that the SIT investigation report gives him a clean chit, Champat Rai Bansal issues a nine-page letter in which Nripendra Misra, chairman of the Ram Temple Construction Committee, comes directly under scrutiny. A member associated with the temple trust says that after the offering theft came to light, Nripendra Misra corners Champat Rai in an interview by raising questions over security arrangements, deletion of CCTV footage and the deployment of more than 1,500 employees. Following this, Champat Rai reportedly distances himself from the controversy and goes into ‘solitude’ at Karsevakpuram in Ayodhya. During this period, his opponents believe that Champat’s influence has weakened. However, he remains quiet and waits for the right opportunity. As soon as the SIT report is presented in court, he launches a direct counter-attack through the letter. Nripendra visits Ayodhya every 15 days, but does not meet Champat Champat Rai also appears upset over Nripendra Misra’s frequent visits to Ayodhya. Misra visits the city roughly every 15 days to attend meetings of the construction committee before returning to Lucknow or Delhi. According to the temple trust member, whenever Nripendra Misra visits Ayodhya, he does not meet Champat Rai. This suggests that the differences between the two are not limited to correspondence and that communication between them has almost broken down. Another dimension of the dispute is their contrasting backgrounds. Nripendra Misra is a former IAS officer, while Champat Rai comes from the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), which has been directly associated with the Ram Temple movement. In his letter, Champat Rai alleges that Nripendra Misra has always considered himself the supreme authority on decisions related to temple construction. He alleges that there is hardly any decision related to the temple's construction that the construction committee does not take on its own. Even when the Trust makes a suggestion, he claims, it is either rejected or the existing construction is removed. The tone of the letter indicates strong objections over the alleged lack of transparency in the selection of companies and financial decisions related to the temple's construction. Champat’s move seen as attempt to limit Misra’s interference Champat Rai's latest move is being viewed as a strategy to limit Nripendra Misra's influence in temple-related affairs. However, construction of the temple is expected to continue until after March 2027. Once the remaining construction work is handed over to the Trust, the Trust itself will decide what role, if any, the construction committee will have. When contacted by Dainik Bhaskar, Nripendra Misra said: I can say something only after seeing the letter. I have not read the letter yet. stories.title: Youth burnt alive after falling into boiling jaggery pan:Struggled for a minute; had gone from Lakhimpur to Maharashtra to earn ₹70,000
stories.summary: 25 year old youth from Lakhimpur died after falling into a pan of boiling jaggery at a jaggery plant in Maharashtra. He remained trapped in the boiling jaggery for nearly a minute and kept crying, “Save me, brother, save me.” Hearing his cries, his colleagues rushed to help and pulled him out after a lot of effort. By then, he had suffered severe burns and his skin had peeled off. He was taken to a hospital, where he died during treatment. The incident took place on 21 August, and the video surfaced around 9 pm on Sunday. The youth had gone to Maharashtra to work and earn money to repay his family’s ₹70,000 debt. See 4 pictures of the accident... Now, read the full story... Had gone to Maharashtra with 15 others for work Danish (25), a resident of Moodi village in Isanagar, Lakhimpur, had been married for two years. About four months ago, he went to Maharashtra with 15 others for work. He is survived by his wife, two month old son, parents, and elder brother and sister. His elder brother, Guddu, had a debt of ₹70,000, which Danish had gone to Maharashtra to help repay. Now, know how the accident happened… 21 August at 2:25 PM, in the plant, jaggery was boiling in two large cauldrons. All the workers were busy with their respective tasks. Danish came and stood right at the edge of the cauldron. After a while, he felt dizzy and lost his balance. In the blink of an eye, he fell straight into the cauldron of boiling jaggery. He screamed loudly, Save me! Save me! Oh brother, save me! There was chaos throughout the entire plant. Fellow workers ran to the cauldron. No one could understand how to get Danish out. Just then, one worker tried to pull him out with a large ladle. Another also picked up a ladle. When he couldn't be pulled out, without caring for their own lives, two three workers stepped forward and pulled him out of the boiling jaggery. They laid him down on the ground away from the cauldron. The skin of his entire body had peeled off. Danish kept screaming due to pain and burning. Some workers shouted, Bring water! Pour water on him! Hurry up! Family created a ruckus in the village, police showed them CCTV footage After receiving information about the accident, Maharashtra Police conducted a post-mortem of the body. After this, the body was sent to Moodi village. As soon as the body reached the village on Saturday, mourning engulfed the family. Family members accused the laborers who had gone to Maharashtra with Danish and started creating a ruckus. Upon receiving information, Isanagar police reached the village. The police showed the family members the CCTV footage from the plant. After watching the footage, the family members calmed down. CO Shamsher Bahadur Singh said, “The incident had occurred at a jaggery plant in Maharashtra. A police team was sent as a precaution when the body reached the village.” He said, “No written complaint has been received against anyone in the matter so far.”

stories.title: Bride flees on fifth day of marriage:Runs off with ₹11 lakh in jewellery and cash; middleman threatens to frame groom’s family in case
stories.summary: A bride fled from her in-laws’ house in Agra just five days after the wedding, taking jewellery and cash worth ₹11 lakh with her. The husband and his family contacted the matchmaker, hoping he might know where she had gone. However, the family alleges that instead of helping them, the middleman threatened to implicate them in a case for allegedly making the woman disappear. According to the family, matchmaker had portrayed the woman as being from a financially weak background and persuaded them to agree to the marriage, saying it would help her build a better life. After the bride disappeared, the husband and his family approached the police to lodge a complaint, but alleged that their complaint was not initially accepted. An FIR has now been registered following a court order. Now, complete matter in detail Guddi Devi, a resident of Awas Vikas Colony Sector-14 in Agra, said that I have three sons. My youngest son Rahul is already married. The search for a match for my eldest son Vishnu's marriage was ongoing. The elder son does flower decoration work. She was looking for a girl for his marriage. She met Jawahar Singh, a resident of Shamsabad. He told her - There is a poor girl named Preeti who lives in Prayagraj. She doesn't have a father. I know her brother. You just have to bear the expenses from both sides. She agreed to the marriage after being convinced by his words. Wedding took place on 27th June Guddi Devi alleges that the young woman's brother, Dhara Singh, demanded ₹1.5 lakh in the name of buying wedding items. The family transferred ₹1 lakh in cash and ₹50,500 online. On 27th June 2026, the wedding rituals were completed at the woman's house, and Preeti started living in the house as a daughter-in-law. Bride suddenly disappeared after 5 days 5 days after the wedding, on the morning of 3rd July, the mother-in-law called her daughter-in-law Preeti for tea. But she was found missing from the house. Guddi Devi said that she searched for her daughter-in-law everywhere. But nothing was found. When checked at home, 4 tolas of gold and 1 kg of silver jewelry were missing. These include two mangalsutras, three gold rings, a silver waistband, and anklets. She also stole ₹16,000 from the ‘Muh dikhai’ ceremony and the younger daughter-in-law's gold ring, mangalsutra, payal, and ₹15,000. The matchmaker Jawahar, said on the phone that you people should not complain to the police. I will bring the girl back. For many days, there was no response from him. Then, he started threatening that he would implicate them in a case of making the girl disappear. After this, the family went to Sikandra police station to file a complaint, but said that the police did not hear their case. An FIR was eventually registered following a court order. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, “Action is being taken based on the evidence. Efforts are underway to trace the bride, who is accused of theft. The matchmaker who arranged the marriage is also being traced.”

stories.title: Yogi tells athletes, 'Win medals, we’ll give jobs':Those who chant 'youth-youth' have no agenda for youth, only mafias
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath arrived at Gorakhnath Temple to watch the wrestling competition organized on the occasion of Nag Panchami in Gorakhpur on Monday afternoon at 3 PM. CM Yogi told the players that we are directly giving jobs to those who win medals for the country. So far, 500 players have been given jobs. The CM said- Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but youth is not in their agenda. They just want to use you. When they were in power, they did nothing for the youth and handed everything over to the mafia. Before this, CM Yogi performed worship of Guru Gorakhnath at Gorakhnath Temple. He went to the samadhi site of Brahmaleen Mahant Avaidyanath and took his blessings. After this, he watched the wrestling matches of the wrestlers. He honored the winning wrestlers. In the presence of the CM, the title matches of Uttar Pradesh Kesari, Uttar Pradesh Kumar and Uttar Pradesh Veer Abhimanyu were held. More than 300 wrestlers participated in this two-day state-level competition. See 2 pictures CM said- If you engage in sports, you will stay away from drugs CM Yogi said that the more youth engage with sports, the more they will stay away from addiction. There are two forms of addiction. One is drugs and intoxicating substances, while the other is smartphone addiction. Today, 90% of the time youth spend on smartphones is wasted. If even one hour from the time spent on smartphones is dedicated to the body, then the body will remain healthy. If the body is healthy, then the mind will also remain healthy. This will enable youth to contribute to making the nation stronger. The first rule for an athlete is self-discipline. They wake up and sleep on time. They follow dietary rules. Old coaches prepared athletes by tempering their lives even with limited resources and without incentives. Today, all kinds of facilities are available for athletes. Government will also help private sports academies; new youth policy soon The CM said that the UP government is soon bringing a new youth policy. Under this, many events and programs will be started for the youth. 'Abhyudaya Coaching' for youth preparing for competitive exams will be extended to every college and university. This facility will be available through both physical and virtual mediums. A 'Skilling and Employment Zone' is being created in every district of the state. Here, under one roof, along with skilling of youth, employment facilities will also be available. If the private sector cooperates in any field of sports, then full support will be provided to it under the state government's sports policy. Strictness against those who play with the future of youth Yogi said that if the copying mafia or education mafia plays with the future of any youth, strict action will be taken against them. Action is also being taken to confiscate the property of such people. He mentioned the sports talents of Ghazipur, saying that Olympic medal winners Lalit Upadhyay and Rajkumar Pal have progressed from Ghazipur's private stadium. He said that this shows that better sports facilities and private academies can play a crucial role in advancing youth. Education, sports and protecting youth from drug mafia is necessary The CM said that old players, wrestlers and coaches dedicated their lives to sports with limited resources and without encouragement. If they had received adequate facilities and encouragement at that time, they could have taken the country's name even further at the international level. He said that sports and youth were not on the agenda of previous governments. Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but while in power they did nothing for the welfare of youth. They handed over the youth power to the mafia. 'Mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power' CM Yogi said that mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power. Whether it is education mafia, sports mafia, drug mafia, or professional criminals, youth suffer the most because of this. To protect youth from this, it is necessary to promote sports and sports culture. The double engine government under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi is working to create a positive environment for sports and youth. He said that a wrestler follows discipline and a sattvic lifestyle. He is also a devotee of Bajrangbali, from whom strength, intelligence, and knowledge are sought..

stories.title: Woman cop who arrested Muskan in 'blue drum case' suspended:Shared videos promoting QR code, was posted at Meerut SSP office
stories.summary: The female inspector who arrested Muskan, accused of dismembering her husband in Meerut, has been suspended. A video related to the officer surfaced on social media on Sunday, following which action was taken against her. The officer, Anu, is originally from Prayagraj and belongs to the 2023 batch of Sub-Inspectors. At the time of the Blue drum case, she was posted at Brahmpuri police station. She was later transferred to the SSP’s office. Anu’s first posting in Meerut was at Rohta police station. Pictures related to the female inspector on social media... YouTuber complained about inspector Anu, says, Yogiji, please A YouTuber had complained about female inspector Anu's objectionable posts on social media. He also released a video to make his point. In which he says- Yogi ji, namaste. Yaar, you can say whatever you want; you are the cutest person. Yogi ji is my most favorite Prime Minister. I mean, it came out wrong from my mouth, but you think about it, I'm going in the right direction, right? Not 29, so what, 34. You'll have my full support, sir. Sir, I wanted to show you a video. Look at this video. I know, Yogi ji, it's the wrong video, and you have a right to be angry. You basically don't pay any attention at all to all these things. This video is of Annie Collis, who is a Sub Inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police. She has Instagram and YouTube channels. She posts reels on them. Some objectionable videos also appear on the YouTube channel. A QR code is also visible along with it. Basically, for donations. You understand the purpose, don't you? This uniform of Uttar Pradesh- if something could be done about its dignity. Now, our DGP sahab, Rajeev Krishna ji. I mean, our country's most important state. One of the most important states is Uttar Pradesh, and its police. If someone sees it, sir. I'm saying, if Haryana police see that, brother, QR codes of Uttar Pradesh police are running at night. I mean, they make a lot of fun on WhatsApp groups internally. You have rules and regulations, right? Steps should be taken against them. There is power; I mean, I don't have it, that's why I allow everything. Do it on Instagram, do it on YouTube too. Just what happens is that the dignity of the uniform falls a little. Yogi ji, Rajiv Krishna ji, let me tell you one thing. Just issue a simple circular, a notification, that police personnel or bureaucrats who are in high positions, who are in good important, significant positions. They should not be allowed to do such dramas on social media or do all this on social media. It looks wrong. It's disrespectful. Whether you believe it or not, dignity falls. Respect falls. Otherwise, great Yogi ji. Big fan. Anu's Instagram account is named Ani Colliss Anu has an account on Instagram with the name Annie Collis. It has 684 posts and 1,016 followers. Sub Inspector Uttar Pradesh Police is written in the profile. It also says, ‘Age Grace My Love’. A YouTube channel link is also attached below. Arrested Muskan in the Blue Drum Saurabh Murder Case Anu is the same woman police officer who arrested and brought accused Muskan in the 2025 Blue Drum murder case. At that time, Anu was posted at Brahmpuri police station. During this time, the famous blue drum case came to light. Anu had also shared a video with Muskan on her social media account. In this video, she can be seen with Muskan. Police will investigate lady inspector's video Action was taken against lady inspector Anu after reports emerged of a violation of the police department's social media policy. Its departmental inquiry has been assigned to CO office officer Saumya Singh. The police will now investigate the reality check of inspector Anu's video along with its source. The team will also find out whether any kind of tampering was done with the lady inspector's video that surfaced on social media. Besides this, facts related to inspector Anu's social media activities will also be investigated. SP Crime Meerut Avneesh Kumar said that in the case of woman sub-inspector Anu, along with a departmental inquiry, an investigation is also being conducted at the cyber level. After the investigation report comes, necessary departmental action will be taken based on the facts. The conduct of the woman sub-inspector falls under the category of violation of the department's social media policy. Such video-related activities while holding a post are wrong. She has been suspended on this basis. The woman sub-inspector's Instagram and YouTube channels are also being investigated. Objectionable videos related to social media have been removed. The woman sub-inspector's account has also been deleted.

stories.title: ATS arrests Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from mosque in Meerut:24-yr-old considered Masood his mentor; made masked videos urging people to wage jihad
stories.summary: UP Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested Mohammad Zafar, a suspected terrorist linked to the Pakistani terrorist organization Jaish-e-Mohammed. This arrest was made on Sunday from a mosque in Meerut. 24-year-old Zafar is a resident of Purnia district in Bihar. He obtained a Maulvi degree from a madrasa in Meerut in 2022. He had come to Meerut just two months ago. ATS issued a press note on Monday. The allegation is that he was collecting donations from people in the name of the madrasa and sending that money to the terrorist organization Jaish-e-Mohammed in Pakistan. During the investigation, evidence of Pakistani jihadi WhatsApp groups and activities related to jihad-caliphate on social media were found on his mobile. During interrogation, Zafar revealed that during his studies he had read about Jaish-e-Mohammed. He was influenced by reading about jihad and the martyrdom of Mujahideen. Coming under the influence of Maulana Masood Azhar, he wanted to become a mujahid. Was influenced by Masood Azhar's speeches According to ATS, Zafar was influenced by the speeches of Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar. He used to share his inflammatory and jihadi speeches to incite people for violent jihad. During the investigation, such activities were found on his social media accounts. On Facebook, he used to post statements related to jihad and caliphate with his face covered. The Pakistani jihadi WhatsApp groups found on Zafar's mobile contained discussions about jihad and donations. Zafar joined this jihadi group of Jaish-e-Mohammed and came in contact with a Pakistani handler. He had also offered to help the handler in jihad. Money sent through binance account According to ATS, Zafar attempted to send money at the behest of a Pakistani handler. After this, he requested information about a Binance account. The suspect remained in contact with Pakistani individuals and sent money multiple times through cryptocurrency USDT. The investigating agency is now gathering information about his contacts, transactions, and other people connected to the terrorist network. ATS has registered an FIR against Zafar. The investigating agency is examining his social media accounts, chats found on his mobile, and contacts linked to Pakistan. Additionally, it is also being investigated where the money was sent through donations and cryptocurrency. Who else besides Zafar is involved in this network? Terrorist Masood Azhar formed JeM 26 years ago Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) is a terrorist organization of Pakistan. It was formed by terrorist Masood Azhar in the year 2000. It is accused of carrying out terrorist attacks in several countries, including India. Jaish's headquarters is in Bahawalpur in Punjab province of Pakistan. This organization operates training camps and terrorist networks in several areas of Pakistan. Its chief terrorist, Masood Azhar, was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir in the year 1994. However, after the hijacking of Indian Airlines flight IC-814 in December 1999, the Government of India released him in exchange for the release of hostages.

stories.title: 8 UP faces, including two Muslims, in BJP’s new team:Three women given key roles; Harish Dwivedi and Basit Ali get promotions
stories.summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin announced his new team at 3 pm on Monday. Six leaders from Uttar Pradesh have been included in the national team, while the presidents of the OBC and Minority Morchas are also from UP. This takes the total number of UP leaders in Nabin’s team to eight. The BJP has formed the team with next year’s Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind. UP has the highest representation of women in the national team among all states, with three leaders: Smriti Irani, Rekha Verma and Sangeeta Yadav. Two leaders from the Pasmanda Muslim community have also been given positions in the national organisation. They include former Aligarh Muslim University Vice-Chancellor Dr. Tariq Mansoor and National Minority Morcha president Kunwar Basit Ali. Mansoor has been reappointed as national vice-president, while Basit Ali has been promoted from his current position as president of the UP BJP Minority Morcha. In terms of caste representation, the team includes one Brahmin, one Parsi, one SC leader and three OBC leaders from the Yadav, Kurmi and Maurya communities. The formation of the team had been pending since Nabin took over as BJP national president seven months ago. Who is close to whom? Find out… Smriti Irani: She is considered one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s close leaders and was a key BJP face against Rahul Gandhi in Amethi. Harish Dwivedi: A former MP from Basti, he is considered close to Home Minister Amit Shah, JP Nadda, and the RSS. He is also regarded as one of the central leadership’s trusted leaders. Rekha Verma: She is considered close to the central leadership and has been reappointed as national vice-president. This is being seen as a sign of her acceptability within the organisation. She is not associated with any particular faction. Tariq Mansoor: He is one of the key figures in the Modi-BJP’s Muslim outreach strategy. As a former AMU vice-chancellor, he has been given another opportunity to help the BJP connect with the Muslim community, particularly the Pasmanda section. Bhola Singh: His inclusion is linked to the party’s central organisation and Dalit strategy. He has been elected MP from Bulandshahr three consecutive times and has worked at the national level in the SC Morcha. His political role is primarily linked to Dalit representation. Sangeeta Yadav: Her husband is an IRS officer. She has stayed away from factional politics and is expected to be useful to the party’s social engineering strategy as both a woman and a Yadav face. Sangeeta Yadav has served as a BJP national secretary. She was an MLA from Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur and is now a Rajya Sabha MP. Amar Pal Maurya: He is considered close to Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya and has also worked with Uma Bharti. Kunwar Basit Ali: He has been associated with the RSS-linked Muslim Rashtriya Manch and has been a prominent face of the BJP’s Muslim outreach campaign. He is considered one of Amit Shah’s trusted leaders. Regional equations were also taken into account Sangeeta Yadav, Harish Dwivedi and Amar Pal Maurya have been given representation from eastern UP. From western UP, Prof Tariq Mansoor, Kunwar Basit Ali and Bhola Singh have been included in the organisation. Rekha Verma from Rohilkhand and Smriti Irani from central UP have also been given positions, ensuring representation across the state. 4 leaders dropped from the organisation Why were UP leaders given importance? Uttar Pradesh is one of the BJP’s most important states, with the 2027 Assembly elections approaching. With 403 Assembly seats, UP has the largest legislative assembly in the country. It also sends 80 MPs to the Lok Sabha. The presence of UP leaders in the BJP’s national organisation could therefore have a direct bearing on the party’s strategy for the upcoming Assembly elections. Regional and social equations are also believed to have influenced the decision to give key responsibilities to leaders from UP. The reappointment of Harish Dwivedi and Rekha Verma to important positions is being seen as an effort to balance the party’s organisational experience with its electoral requirements. UP has highest representation with 3 women in Nitin Nabin’s team BJP president Nitin Nabin’s new national team has given responsibilities to 12 women. They include General Secretary Smriti Irani, Vice-President Rekha Verma and National Secretary Sangeeta Yadav. With three women, Uttar Pradesh has the highest representation in the team. Maharashtra has two women, while the remaining states have one woman each. Nitin became BJP president 209 days ago Nitin Nabin became the BJP’s national president 209 days ago, replacing JP Nadda. He was elected unopposed and, at 45, became the BJP’s youngest-ever national president.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft:SIT report cannot be shared with outsiders, Solicitor General tells SC; court asks for sealed copy
stories.summary: The Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case was heard in the Supreme Court on Monday afternoon. The petitioners’ lawyers asked the court to provide them with the investigation report so they could assist in the proceedings. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta opposed the request, saying the report could not be shared with people who were not directly connected with the case. The petitioners’ lawyer responded that they were not strangers and that the plea had been filed on behalf of the people of India. The lawyer argued that they had a fundamental right to know the truth. He said that if investigation-related information had been shared with an accused or someone assisting the probe while the petitioners were kept out, they would not be able to effectively assist the court. On this, the Supreme Court made a stern remark saying - We have constituted the SIT. It is answerable and accountable to the court. It has to submit its report to us only. The SIT with a forensic auditor should file its status report in a sealed cover in the Supreme Court. We will see the report first. After that, we will decide whether to hand it over to all parties or not. The bench of Chief Justice (CJI) Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing petitions demanding a CBI investigation into the theft of offerings. Earlier, on 27 July, the court had directed the inclusion of a forensic auditor in the SIT to examine accounts and records to detect financial irregularities. On 20 July, the court had ordered the UP government to constitute a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT). Court room LIVE Supreme Court: The petitioner or any other well-intentioned person with a public-interest spirit can give their suggestions to the Solicitor General's office. These suggestions can be about aspects that need thorough investigation by the SIT. Petitioner's Lawyer: We should be given a copy of the investigation report so that we can assist the court. Solicitor General: The investigation report cannot be shared with any unknown person or external party. Petitioner's Lawyer: We are not unknown. This petition has been filed on behalf of the people of India. We have a fundamental right to know the truth. Petitioner's Lawyer: I would like to place one matter before you. This case is pending before this court, and the Chief Minister is publicly citing the SIT (Special Investigation Team) findings and saying that no sadhu is involved in this. Chief Justice: If the SIT is doing its work satisfactorily, then that is a different matter. But, if you feel that there is some deficiency in their work and it needs improvement, then our stance is open. We can issue new guidelines. Earlier, Vijay Vishwas Pant's SIT had conducted the investigation
