stories.title: Nripendra Misra reacts to Champat Rai’s allegations:Calls it 'media’s fabricated story for controversy'; Champat had accused him of acting arbitrarily
stories.summary: Tensions between former IAS officer Nripendra Misra and Champat Rai appear to be deepening following the Ram Mandir donation-theft case. On Friday, when reporters in Ayodhya questioned Misra about Champat Rai's allegations of high-handedness, he reacted with irritation. He said, I have not seen any such letter. Until I see the letter, I will maintain that this is a media-concocted story. You people only want to create controversy — that's why you're asking me this question. There may be a nine-page letter, but even so, he (Champat Rai) would not have criticised in this manner. Champat Rai's nine-page letter surfaced on Thursday, making several claims about the role of Nripendra Misra, chairman of the temple construction committee. In the letter, Rai alleged high-handedness, claiming Misra had inducted people of his own choosing into the construction committee. Champat Rai had resigned as general secretary on 26 June, after the donation-theft case came to light. His resignation was accepted at a trust meeting on 6 July. What Champat Rai's letter said Champat Rai said the trust set up for the Ram Mandir's construction had 15 trustees, with Nripendra Misra appointed chairman of the construction committee. He alleged that on Misra's recommendation, Larsen Toubro (LT) was given responsibility for the temple's construction, and Noida-based firm Design Associates was selected for work related to the design and construction of the buildings. He alleged Misra inducted people of his choosing into the construction committee, some of whom visited Ayodhya only once or twice in six years, while former NBCC chairman Anoop Mittal regularly attended construction committee meetings alongside Misra. "Priority given to Nripendra Misra's decisions" Champat Rai wrote that decisions related to the temple's construction were taken at committee meetings, but in several cases were later changed, with priority given to Misra's decisions. He alleged that suggestions or decisions from other committee members were, in several cases, not given due importance. "Struggle for Ram Mandir construction ran from 1528 to 2019" In 1528, Babur's forces demolished the Ram Janmabhoomi temple. Following this, a struggle to reclaim the temple land continued among Ayodhya's seers, local rulers and princely states, and the general public. In 1949, the local community took possession of the site, after which this phase of the struggle ended. Between 1950 and 1989, four suits were filed in local courts, which were fought independently by those who filed them. The case was later heard by a three-judge bench of the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court. Over roughly 15 years of hearings, the three judges wrote independent verdicts running to a combined total of about 8,500 pages. The Supreme Court attempted a negotiated settlement through a three-member mediation panel. Several rounds of talks were held between March and July 2019, but no resolution was reached. A five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court then began regular hearings from 6 August 2019, delivering a unanimous verdict on 9 November 2019 that cleared the way for the temple's construction. Following the Supreme Court's direction, the central government constituted an independent trust named Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, comprising 15 trustees, with one seat reserved for the Nirmohi Akhara and one for SC/ST representation. IAS officers representing the Ayodhya DM, the Uttar Pradesh government, and the central government were made ex-officio trustees. Construction-related suggestions from the late VHP leader Ashok Singhal were conveyed to Nripendra Misra. LT was selected for the temple's construction, with Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) appointed to oversee it. Noida-based Design Associates and its principal, Jai Kaktikar, were given responsibility for designing the other buildings in the temple complex. Champat Rai also referred to arrangements for darshan at the Ram Mandir A Yatri Seva Kendra has been built on Ram Path opposite Birla Dharamshala, on what was earlier a UP State Road Transport Corporation bus stand; the trust purchased the land and built a two-storey prefabricated structure there. Since the pran-pratishtha of Ramlala on 22 January 2024, more than 75,000 devotees have been visiting daily, with numbers exceeding 3 lakh a day during the Maha Kumbh. Eight queues have been set up for Ramlala darshan — one VIP line, one easy-access/wheelchair line and six general lines — each with separate routes to avoid crossing. General darshan continues even during VIP visits, with separate arrangements for the governor, chief minister, Union ministers and judges. Free wheelchairs are available for devotees with disabilities, and free arrangements are made in the complex for bhajans, kirtans and Sundarkand recitations. The trust's bank accounts do not use chequebooks; all payments are made via bank transfer, with no cash payments. The trust holds accounts with SBI, PNB and Bank of Baroda, and its financial transactions undergo both internal and statutory audits, with the statutory audit conducted by Delhi-based firm V. Sankar Aiyar.

stories.title: SP leader says Meerut SSP beat him with boots:Swollen eye, multiple injuries; allegedly threatened, ‘You’ll do politics wearing a ₹40 kurta?’
stories.summary: In Meerut, Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Dr Digvijay Bhati has accused SSP Avinash Pandey, who was recently in the news for allegedly slapping protesters during demonstrations over the Lalita Gautam murder case, of assaulting him and his colleague Mohit Jatav. Bhati alleged that the SSP abused both of them inside his chamber and then severely assaulted them. He claimed the SSP repeatedly kicked them with his boots, leaving him with serious internal injuries and a swollen eye. According to Bhati, the SSP also threatened them and taunted them for ‘trying to act like politicians while wearing a ₹40 kurta’. After the alleged assault, Civil Lines in-charge Akhilesh Gaur and other policemen reportedly took the two men to the Special Operations Group (SOG) office. Bhati alleged that they were taken into a closed room, tied by their hands and feet and beaten with sticks. The SP leader later released a video showing injury marks on his body and making the allegations. The incident reportedly took place on Wednesday, August 19, while the video surfaced late Thursday night. Meanwhile, SSP Avinash Pandey has been removed from his post and attached to Police Headquarters. He had served as Meerut’s police chief for around six months, reportedly making it the shortest tenure of any Meerut SSP in the past 10 years. What the SP leader alleged against SSP and Inspector Dr. Digvijay Bhati, President of Bhartiya Kisan Union BR Ambedkar, stated, On August 19, our District President Mohit and I went to meet the SSP. In connection with the protest against the Lalita Gautam murder case, the police had sent 8-10 of us to jail. Since we were not at fault, nor were we involved in the protest, we went to the Captain (SSP) to present our case. When we met the SSP, he became agitated and, using abusive language, started saying, You wear a 40-rupee kurta-pajama and become leaders, will you clash with us? When we protested against the abuse, the SSP dragged us into his chamber and beat us with kicks, punches, and shoes.After this, we were taken to the SOG office, where Civil Lines Inspector Akhilesh and his colleagues severely tortured us. We were released at 2 AM when SP leader Atul Pradhan arrived. A condition was set that if the matter came to the media, we would be treated worse. Panic among senior officers upon receiving information According to sources, when senior officers came to know about the incident, there was a stir in the department. Taking cognizance of the matter, Avinash Pandey was removed from Meerut and attached to the police headquarters at the government level last night. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said, The heinous act committed by BJP of kicking a farmer in the face and threatening farmers across the country is unforgivable. This shows how rattled they are by the fear of defeat. 'Followed Captain Sahab's orders' Inspector Akhilesh Kumar Gaur told Dainik Bhaskar in a conversation that he reached there later and followed the order given to him by Captain Sahab. When an attempt was made to contact Avinash Pandey regarding the matter, he did not pick up the phone. Avinash Pandey's old connection with controversies Avinash Pandey has been involved in controversies multiple times in Meerut itself. Incidents of misbehavior with a senior advocate had also come to light. During his posting in Pilibhit, Avinash Pandey was also involved in an assault incident at a guesthouse. Similarly, during his posting in Mau, when Avinash Pandey was traveling to Prayagraj by train for a case, an incident of assault with an attendant had also come to light. stories.title: Lucknow murder case:Manager wife demanded ₹1.5 crore, wanted to live separately from sister-in-law; SBI officer killed entire family in 30 minutes
stories.summary: Lucknow police say an SBI officer carried out two murders and killed himself within 30 minutes, after allegedly surveilling his estranged wife for two days. Initial investigation has pointed to two possible motives: bank manager Divya Mishra had sought ₹1.5 crore in alimony from her husband, SBI officer Manas Bajpai, during divorce proceedings, and she did not want to live with his mentally ill sister, Sheeba. According to police sources, a hearing in the couple's divorce case was held in family court on 18 August, during which a dispute reportedly broke out between Manas and Divya over the alimony demand. Police say Manas grew increasingly disturbed after this and began planning to kill his wife and sister before taking his own life. He allegedly bought three firearms and surveilled Divya for two days. On Thursday afternoon, around 12 pm, Manas reportedly arrived by auto-rickshaw at the ICICI Bank branch where Divya worked and called her outside. Police say the two argued and there was a physical altercation, after which Manas shot her twice in the face. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed outside the bank. He then reportedly fled the scene in the same auto-rickshaw and reached his home, about 2 km away. Police say he shut himself in a room, played the Hanuman Chalisa loudly on television, then shot his sister Sheeba in the head before shooting himself. Divya was the sister of YouTuber Pragya Mishra, who has alleged that her brother-in-law was "psycho" and that her sister kept her distance from him for this reason. Manas and Divya had married for love nine years ago. Read the full story See 2 pictures related to the murder Love marriage nine years ago, wife left home a year ago According to family members, Manas and Divya married in 2017 and their relationship was reportedly fine in the initial years, but disputes over minor issues began later, leading to growing distance between them. In 2018, when Manas's mother was diagnosed with cancer, Divya reportedly moved back in with him. Around this time, disputes are said to have started between the couple over living with Manas's sister. After his mother's death in 2019, Divya reportedly separated again, before the two later reconciled. In 2025, the dispute over the sister reportedly resurfaced, with Divya saying she did not want to live with her, while Manas was said to be unwilling to agree. Divya reportedly moved out completely in November 2025. Manas is said to have tried to save the marriage and spoke to Divya several times, but the matter eventually reached Lucknow family court. Divya filed a case in the family court in January 2026, beginning the legal divorce process. Bought three weapons, began surveilling wife A friend of Manas told police he had been out of the city for around three months for bank audit work. After returning, he reportedly learnt of the 18 August family court hearing and attended it, where police say he learnt of the ₹1.5 crore alimony demand, which allegedly left him stressed. According to the police investigation, after the 18 August hearing, Manas planned to kill his wife and sister and then take his own life. He is said to have arranged three weapons — reportedly two 9mm pistols and a country-made pistol — over two days. Police have recovered all three weapons, all of which were loaded. Where and from whom he obtained them is still under investigation, after which he allegedly began surveilling Divya. Called wife over, allegedly beat then shot her Divya's cousin, Mayank Dixit, said that on 20 August, Divya had gone out for bank work and, upon returning to office by car in the afternoon, found Manas already present. He reportedly signalled to her and said he wanted to talk. When Divya approached him, Manas allegedly began assaulting her. Bank guards and staff reportedly rushed to help her, during which Manas allegedly shot her in the forehead. Divya collapsed on the road, after which Manas fled the scene. He is then said to have gone straight to his home, about 2 km away, where he allegedly shot his sister Sheeba dead before shooting himself. CCTV footage of the entire sequence has also emerged. WhatsApp status before suicide alleged wife "betrayed" him Police say Manas put up a WhatsApp status after killing his wife, in which he accused her of betrayal and wrote about killing himself and his sister. The status reportedly also mentioned Divya's sister Pragya and her husband, Bharat Yadav. Mayank Dixit said Pragya and Bharat had no knowledge of any such plan, and that Manas's behaviour had not seemed normal for some time. Police are also investigating the claims made in the status. Divya was living with parents, Manas lived with sister in rented house After separating from Manas, Divya had been living at her parental home in Shringar Nagar, Alambagh. She had recently built a house in Buddheshwar, Para, where she was living with her parents at the time. Her father is a retired government employee, while her mother is a homemaker. Manas lived in a rented house near Husadiya Chauraha with his sister, Sheeba Bajpai (28). He worked as a field officer at SBI's engineering college branch. His father, also a bank employee, died around six years ago; his mother has since died as well. Pragya alleges Manas was also involved in mother's death YouTuber Pragya Mishra wrote on X, alleging that her sister had told her Manas and his sister had beaten their ailing mother so severely that she died. She alleged her brother-in-law was "psycho" and had stalked Divya before. She said Divya had been in an accident some time earlier due to stress, breaking her arm and leg, and had only returned to work after a month and a half, still limping. Pragya wrote that everyone who knew Divya was aware of what she had endured, and that she felt this was an important time to speak out despite her grief. "He was cruel to my sister," Pragya alleges Pragya alleged that on their wedding night, Manas had drawn up a list of household expenses and insisted Divya pay half, which she had agreed to. She alleged he was cruel to her sister, including berating her over spoiled tomatoes ordered through a delivery app. She said Divya had stopped paying her share of expenses over the past year, which she believed Manas may have viewed as a betrayal, while Divya had simply wanted to separate from him. Pragya said her sister had told her there had been a confrontation between Manas and a counsellor during family court proceedings. "She wanted things to be fine, hoped he would change" Pragya said she had known her brother-in-law was cruel to her sister and that this was why Divya wanted to separate, but she had not anticipated he would take such a drastic step. She said that despite everything, Divya had still planned to observe the Teej fast and had not removed a tattoo of Manas's name, saying she had hoped, deep down, that things would work out. Pragya said she had not been able to bring herself to tell their mother that Divya had been killed, telling her instead that her condition was critical, and that this was the first time she had realised how difficult it was to speak the truth.

stories.title: Yogi govt gives bulletproof jackets to Akhilesh, Mayawati:44 leaders receive ₹10 lakh jackets; minister says, ‘We don’t know how to wear them’
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government has provided bulletproof jackets to 44 leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The list includes 11 Cabinet ministers. Ministers Sanjay Nishad, Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’ and OP Rajbhar have received the jackets. The bulletproof jackets have been purchased by the UP government’s Security Headquarters. Each jacket reportedly costs around ₹10 lakh. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Minister Sanjay Nishad confirmed that he had received one. However, he said he did not know how to wear it and had not yet been trained to use it. According to sources, the government has taken the precautionary step keeping the 2027 Assembly elections in mind. This is reportedly the first time that bulletproof jackets have been provided to political leaders. The government has not officially disclosed why the jackets are being distributed. However, sources said 98 leaders in Uttar Pradesh currently have security cover under different categories, of whom 44 have been provided with bulletproof jackets. The list is not limited to ministers and prominent opposition leaders. BJP’s firebrand western UP leaders Sangeet Som and Suresh Rana are also among those receiving the jackets. Rana is an MLA, while Som currently holds no political post. This has led to speculation that the jackets may have been issued based on intelligence inputs. 98 people have security cover in UP, 12 have Z-plus security These ministers have Y-plus security Sanjay Nishad gets Y-category security State Fisheries Minister Sanjay Nishad has been provided Y-category security with an escort. The same security cover has been given to Pankaj Singh, son of Rajnath Singh; former Governor Kalraj Mishra; former Governor Phagu Chauhan; State Women’s Commission vice-chairperson Aparna Bisht Yadav; former DGP and BJP Rajya Sabha MP Brij Lal; Rajveer Singh, son of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh; Pooja Pal, MLA from Chail in Kaushambi; and Santosh Das, popularly known as Satua Baba, the mahant of Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Overall, 10 people have Y-plus security, 26 have Y-category security, and 17 have X-category security.

stories.title: ₹1.40 crore worth of hydroponic cannabis seized in Gorakhpur:5 smugglers arrested; consignment was to be supplied to clubs and discos in Gujarat
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Ramgarhtal police, in a joint operation with the Anti Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) and Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), have arrested five alleged smugglers and uncovered an interstate network involved in supplying hydroponic ‘OG’ cannabis from Thailand to Delhi and then Gujarat. Cannabis allegedly supplied to Gujarat clubs and discos According to sources, the high-value cannabis was allegedly being smuggled into Gujarat and supplied to clubs and discos, where it was sold to young people at premium prices. 3.085kg cannabis worth Rs 1.40 crore seized The five suspects were arrested late on Wednesday (19 Aug) night in the Ramgarhtal area. Police recovered 3.085 kg of hydroponic cannabis, estimated by ANTF to be worth around ₹1.40 crore. An Ertiga car, five mobile phones and ₹30,390 in cash were also seized. The accused are residents of Pratapgarh and Gujarat. 3kg hydroponic cannabis recovered from Ertiga during search SP City Nimish Patil said, “The joint ANTF and UP ATS team intercepted an Ertiga bearing registration number GJ-15 AA-8841 near the LIC office on Deoria Bypass late on Wednesday, August 19. During a search of the vehicle, officers recovered hydroponic ‘OG’ cannabis from the accused.” Thailand consignment allegedly routed through Delhi to Gujarat During interrogation, the accused allegedly revealed that the hydroponic cannabis sourced from Thailand was being transported to Gujarat via Delhi. In Surat and Bhavnagar, the cannabis was allegedly divided into smaller packets and sold to users at high prices. Investigators also suspect that supplies were delivered to clubs and discos based on demand. Cannabis allegedly collected from vehicle in Deoria The arrested suspects have been identified as Suraj Singh and Satyam Singh of Karmahi village in Kandhai, Pratapgarh; Prince Patel of Grid Road, Navsari; Ratnam Trivedi of Katargam, Surat; and Bhavin of Daman Chowk, Bhavnagar. During questioning, the accused allegedly told investigators that a youth had supplied the OG cannabis in a vehicle bearing a Deoria registration number. His identity and address have not yet been established. ATS and ANTF teams have also found indications pointing to foreign links in the suspected smuggling network. Investigation underway to trace Thailand-India route Investigators are now trying to establish how the cannabis allegedly travelled from Thailand to India and identify the channels used to transport it further. The accused's mobile phones are being examined to trace their contacts and the wider network. The ANTF Gorakhpur unit in-charge has lodged an FIR for alleged drug trafficking at Ramgarhtal police station.

stories.summary: More than ₹100 crore is being lost to cyber fraud in Uttar Pradesh every month. Shocking figures from the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) show that over 2.5 lakh complaints were received in the state in the past seven months, but FIRs were registered in only 1,040 cases. Police managed to arrest just 1,957 accused. Instead of hacking mobile phones or computers, cyber fraudsters are now hacking people’s minds. They exploit fear, greed, romance and sympathy to trap victims. From educated young people to senior citizens, victims have lost more than ₹720 crore to such frauds. Timely intervention helped freeze ₹242 crore, but ₹478 crore reached the fraudsters. Here is how the four major cyber fraud models work: 1. Digital arrest: Fraudsters exploit fear of police action In this model, fraudsters pose as police officers or officials from investigative agencies and threaten victims with legal action. According to the NCRP, such cases may be fewer in UP, but they accounted for around 23% of the money lost to cyber fraud in the seven months. In July, a senior citizen couple in Lucknow was kept under ‘digital arrest’ for nearly seven days. The fraudsters posed as senior officials of an investigative agency and claimed that a SIM card issued in the couple’s name had been used for terrorist activities in Kashmir and money laundering. The couple became so frightened that they locked themselves in a room at home. The fraudsters remained connected with them through video calls and continuously issued instructions. They even controlled when the couple slept, woke up and ate. Under pressure, the couple broke fixed deposits and transferred their life savings. They ended up transferring ₹70 lakh to the fraudsters’ bank accounts. 2. Greed: Fake investment schemes promise quick profits This model generally begins with a phone call or social media message. Victims are persuaded to transfer money through UPI. It is the most common model in UP, accounting for 32% of cases. A recent case was reported from Kanpur on 16 August. Rajaram Shakyawar was added to a social media group and promised high returns from the stock market. The fraudsters claimed to be associated with a registered security company. They first shared stock market information to gain his trust and then persuaded him to invest in IPOs and FPOs. He transferred ₹6.5 lakh. When Rajaram tried to withdraw the money, the fraudsters demanded more deposits. Realising he had been duped, he filed a complaint on the cybercrime portal. Kalyanpur Police are investigating the bank accounts, mobile numbers, website and financial transactions linked to the case. 3. Nude video calls: Threat of public shame used to extort money Around 9–10% of cyber fraud cases follow this model. Many victims hesitate to report such crimes because they fear social embarrassment. On 6 April, a retired sub-inspector from Bhogaon in Mainpuri was targeted through a romance scam. A woman first called him on WhatsApp and claimed to be a relative. She then made a video call and suddenly appeared nude when he answered. He immediately ended the call. Around 40 minutes later, she called again, claiming that her mother was ill and she needed ₹1 lakh. She threatened to make the video call recording public if he did not pay. The retired officer refused. The next day, he received an edited video on WhatsApp showing him apparently speaking to the woman while she was nude. Fearing public humiliation, he transferred around ₹3.47 lakh to the bank account provided by the fraudster. 4. Impersonation: Fraudsters hack accounts and ask contacts for money In June, Dr Himani Agrawal, a member of the Uttar Pradesh State Commission for Women, had her WhatsApp account hacked. The fraudsters began messaging people in her contact list, including police officers, doctors and others. Posing as Dr Agrawal, they asked for ₹45,000, ₹50,000 and ₹52,000. Some people even transferred money. The fraud was exposed when people who knew Dr Agrawal called her to confirm the requests. Such cases account for around 5% of cyber fraud in UP. One reason the success rate is lower is that people often call the person directly to verify the request, preventing the fraud. Cyber expert: Fraudsters create pressure to make victims act quickly Cybersecurity expert Rakshit Tandon, who trains Uttar Pradesh Police personnel in cyber technology, says fraudsters use one tactic regardless of the method: they pressure victims into making an immediate decision. They repeatedly tell victims that they have only five minutes to act — otherwise a case will be registered, a parcel will be seized or their bank account will be permanently blocked. This leaves victims with little time to think, speak to their family or contact the relevant department. They make decisions under fear and pressure, which is exactly what fraudsters exploit. Tandon advises victims not to panic if they lose money to cyber fraud. The first hour should be treated as the ‘golden hour’. Victims should immediately call the national cybercrime helpline 1930. The sooner a complaint is filed, the greater the chance of putting the money on hold or recovering it. Children and young people are also being targeted Cyber fraudsters are increasingly targeting children and young people through gaming, fake APK files and investment scams. Gaming apps: Free coins can empty bank accounts Children are offered free coins, rewards or new characters in online games. They may then be asked to download an app or click on a link. In some cases, children also share passwords or OTPs received on their parents’ phones. Fraudsters can then withdraw money from the linked bank account within minutes. Fake APK files: Wedding invitations and challans used to hack phones Fraudsters send APK files through WhatsApp or SMS, disguising them as wedding invitations, traffic challan updates or documents containing confidential information. Once a person downloads and installs the file, malware can enter the phone. This allows fraudsters to gain control of the device and steal OTPs and other sensitive information. Fake trading and crypto schemes: Promises of 500% returns Fraudsters create fake trading and cryptocurrency groups on Telegram and Instagram, promising returns of up to 500%. They initially show fake profits on an app or account to gain the victim’s trust. Once the victim is convinced, they are encouraged to invest larger amounts. Young people who have recently started working are particularly vulnerable as they can be drawn in by promises of quick money and end up losing their savings.

stories.title: How responsive are UP DMs, SPs to common people?:Bhaskar called officials in all 75 districts, only 3 answered; know the reality
stories.summary: Most government officials in Uttar Pradesh appear to be unavailable to members of the public — either attending meetings or participating in video conferences. Many district magistrates (DMs) and senior police officers do not answer calls made to their official numbers themselves. Instead, their official phones are often with public relations officers (PROs) or stenographers, who decide whether a caller can speak to the officer. This is despite government rules requiring DMs, SPs and SSPs to keep their official mobile phones with them and answer public calls themselves. The government spends crores of rupees every year to keep these official numbers operational so that people can seek quick solutions to their problems. The police department alone spends around ₹9 crore a year on recharges for its official CUG numbers. Yet, officers often appear reluctant to speak to people over the phone. MPs and MLAs have repeatedly raised complaints about this with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. But do officers really fail to answer their official numbers? To find out, Dainik Bhaskar called the official numbers of DMs and police chiefs in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Since officers could be busy at different times, calls were made three times a day — at 11 am, 3 pm and 6 pm. Now, let's tell you sequentially what responses were received where 72 of 75 DMs did not answer calls Of the 75 DMs contacted, 72 did not answer the calls themselves. In several districts, the PRO answered the phone, while in some cases the number could not be reached. Only three DMs directly answered the call and explained how the problem could be addressed. The situation was worse with the police chiefs. Not a single SP or SSP spoke directly over the phone. In Moradabad, the SSP’s PRO even asked whether the caller had used any “source” or contact to get through to the officer. Here is what Bhaskar found across the districts: In 25 districts, the answer was: ‘DM is in a meeting’ In Firozabad, Mainpuri, Mathura, Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat, Ayodhya, Sultanpur, Gorakhpur, Maharajganj, Lalitpur, Banda, Bahraich, Balrampur, Shravasti, Saharanpur, Rae Bareli, Meerut, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Baghpat, Bulandshahr, Hapur, Shahjahanpur, Basti, Hathras and Pratapgarh, the person answering the phone gave the same response: The officer is in a meeting or video conference. In 14 districts, assistants offered alternatives In Agra, Jhansi, Jalaun, Kannauj, Kaushambi, Mirzapur, Gonda, Bareilly, Lucknow, Chandauli, Azamgarh, Varanasi and Sonbhadra, the PRO or stenographer did not connect the caller to the DM. Instead, they suggested visiting the tehsil or sub-divisional magistrate (SDM), or coming to the office the next day with a written complaint. Some were ‘busy with guests’, others had switched-off phones In Kushinagar, the DM’s PRO said guests had arrived and the officer was busy. In Farrukhabad, Chitrakoot and Pilibhit, callers were told: “The DM is busy. Come to the office tomorrow.” In Shamli, the PRO suggested sending the complaint on WhatsApp instead of connecting the caller to the DM. In Prayagraj, the DM’s PRO said the CUG number was meant only for emergencies and that the officer was at the High Court. However, the government rules allow members of the public to contact officials on their official numbers. The CUG numbers of the DMs in Ambedkar Nagar, Ghaziabad and Kasganj were switched off. In Deoria, Etah, Amethi and Siddharthnagar, the numbers repeatedly showed messages such as “out of network coverage area” or “not reachable”. In 21 districts, the phone kept ringing In Unnao, Amroha, Mahoba, Hardoi, Sitapur, Barabanki, Moradabad, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Bhadohi, Jaunpur, Fatehpur, Badaun, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Rampur, Sant Kabir Nagar, Sambhal, Hamirpur and Aligarh, the phone kept ringing, but no responsible officer or staff member answered. Only three districts offered a solution In Etawah, DM Shubhrant Kumar Shukla answered the official number himself. He listened to the problem and advised the caller to first approach the tehsil. He said he would personally look into the matter if it was not resolved there. In Auraiya, the DM was on leave for official reasons, but Additional District Magistrate (ADM) Brijesh Kumar answered the CUG number. He listened to the problem and offered help. In Lakhimpur Kheri, DM Anjani Kumar Singh answered the call himself and asked the caller to send the complaint directly on WhatsApp, providing a simple way to register the grievance. What happened when Bhaskar called the police chiefs? Bhaskar called the official numbers of 68 SPs/SSPs and seven police commissioners across Uttar Pradesh. Not a single police chief spoke directly. Three police chiefs had switched-off phones The official numbers of the SPs in Hapur, Mirzapur and Sant Kabir Nagar were switched off. Calls went unanswered in 16 districts Calls to the official numbers of the police chiefs in Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Baghpat, Ballia, Barabanki, Bijnor, Ghazipur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Jhansi, Kannauj, Kanpur Dehat, Mahoba, Mau, Saharanpur and Shravasti went unanswered. Only two offices called back The SP offices in Maharajganj and Sonbhadra called back later. However, even there, the PRO spoke to the caller instead of the SP. The response was the same: “The officer is busy. We will get you connected later.” Assistants answered in 54 districts In 54 districts, assistants answered the calls and said the police chief was busy in a meeting and might be available later. When Bhaskar called again, however, the officer was still not connected. Strange responses from Kushinagar and Moradabad In Kushinagar, PRO Mahendra Prajapati, speaking on behalf of SP Keshav Kumar, said the officer did not speak to people over the phone. He asked callers to visit the public grievance hearing between 10 am and 2 pm or tell him their problem. In Moradabad, the SSP’s PRO asked: “Are you an officer? Have you got someone to call on your behalf to speak to the sahib?” He added that the SSP did not speak to people directly over the phone. What do the rules say about official numbers? In November 2020, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered all DMs, SPs and SSPs to keep their official mobile phones with them and answer calls from the public themselves. The order also prohibited officers from handing over their official phones to PAs, PROs, gunmen or subordinate staff. The Chief Minister’s Office can randomly call officers on their official numbers to check whether they are answering calls themselves. Failure to answer or return missed calls can be treated as indiscipline and neglect of public grievances, with departmental action possible. On 15 March 2021, then Director General of Police Hitesh Chandra Awasthi also issued a strict circular directing all police chiefs, commissioners, DIGs and IGs to keep their official numbers with them. Police spends ₹9 crore a year on CUG numbers The Uttar Pradesh Police has around 25,000 CUG SIM cards, most of them operated through BSNL. The state’s 2026-27 Budget provides around ₹9 crore for keeping these numbers active and paying for data and other recharges. The department declined to disclose the expenditure on CUG connections issued to district magistrates. The Bhaskar investigation raises a basic question: if official numbers are meant to give citizens direct access to senior officers, why are so few officers answering those calls themselves?

An internal probe uncovered suspicious use of the automated license-plate reader system. Following his surrender, prosecutors agreed to dismiss charges, igniting debate over the access and use of police surveillance tools.

50 years ago, this California sanctuary began saving some of the world’s rarest gibbons
stories.summary: Nestled north of Los Angeles, a gibbon sanctuary has championed the protection of endangered species for five decades. Established in 1976, this facility currently houses roughly forty primates of five diverse species. Beyond managing breeding initiatives, it facilitates animal exchanges and pursues non-invasive research while educating college students about animal husbandry. Looking ahead, the sanctuary seeks funding to enhance living spaces and develop an education center for visitors.

Exhausted owl stranded 70 miles offshore tries to board British Army boat, sailors bring it ashore
stories.summary: A British Army sailing crew found an exhausted barn owl 70 nautical miles from shore during the RORC Round Britain and Ireland Race. The bird fell into the sea three times before managing to reach their boat and collapsing on the deck. The sailors cared for the owl, named Little Regina, until a lifeboat took it back to land for treatment at a wildlife centre.

'There won't be a teleprompter': Sanjay Raut dares PM Modi, Shah to sing full Vande Mataram
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut challenged Prime Minister Modi and Amit Shah to sing Vande Mataram without teleprompters. He also questioned the government's economic record and rising inflation. The BJP condemned the Congress decision to sing only two stanzas of the national song. Congress leaders accused the BJP of politicizing patriotism and nationalism for political gain. Both parties are trading charges over the national song's recitation and its significance.

stories.title: Her ‘picture-perfect’ home has now become a burden
stories.summary: Residents in the Faroe Islands face challenges as tourists treat their homes like exhibits. Visitors often disregard private boundaries, peeking into windows and leaning on fences. This constant intrusion disrupts daily life and erodes personal privacy for homeowners. The article highlights the need for responsible tourism and respecting local residents' lives. Beauty should not become a burden, and visitors must show intention and respect.

stories.title: 'Party of loudmouths': CM Devendra Fadnavis says Rahul Gandhi's Pune event for women a 'showoff'
stories.summary: CM Devendra Fadnavis attacked the Congress, accusing the party of losing touch with voters and relying on public statements to remain politically relevant. "Their job is just to make speeches every day and stay relevant through television; that's all they do. They have lost touch with the ground. This party is limited to merely issuing statements," he claimed.

stories.title: New Zealand removed 200,000 mice from an island; native bird populations more than doubled
stories.summary: New Zealand's 2016 effort to remove an estimated 200,000 mice from Antipodes Island has been followed by a clear recovery in native bird populations. Monitoring confirmed the mice were gone in 2018, while surveys over the next six years found Antipodes Island pipit and snipe numbers had more than doubled.

Explainer: What will actually change for you under UCC
Pakistan power crisis: Karachi residents riot amid outages lasting hours, block major roads
stories.summary: Residents of Karachi voiced their frustrations over persistent power outages by staging protests that blocked major thoroughfares. These demonstrations, which unfolded in various neighborhoods, led to significant traffic disruptions. Many participants reported enduring daily power cuts that lasted twelve hours or longer, with no prior notice. The ongoing electricity crisis worsened issues with water supply and local businesses.

stories.title: How Texas turned an abandoned golf course into five lakes to control flood
stories.summary: Exploration Green in Clear Lake City, Texas, transformed a former golf course into a 200-acre green space with stormwater detention lakes, wetlands and recreation areas. The project was created to help reduce flooding in the community, with its five planned detention lakes capable of storing 500 million gallons of water.

stories.title: 'Words being put in my mouth': Deepender Hooda denies calling Sajjan Kumar a 'role model'
Apollo 15 astronauts found green glass beads on the Moon; decades later, they revealed evidence of water inside
stories.summary: Apollo 15 astronauts found unusual green flecks on the Moon's surface. These flecks were later identified as volcanic glass beads containing trapped water. Researchers discovered hydrogen within these tiny beads, proving lunar water existed. This finding challenged the long-held belief that the Moon was extremely dry. The discovery revealed significant water presence deep within the Moon's interior.

stories.title: Florida teen tests AI bias: Just 17.4% of images showed women scientists
Hindu family of four found dead in locked home in Bangladesh’s Rangpur; strangulation suspected
stories.summary: A chilling scene unfolded when police discovered the bodies of four members of a Hindu family in their locked home. Initial investigations point to strangulation and a possible robbery. The family's absence since Thursday and the lack of phone activity raised alarm. Following a forced entry, officers located the victims throughout the house. Autopsy results are pending to establish the precise cause of their untimely deaths.

stories.title: Meet John Liu, the student who used corn stalks to recover lithium from water
stories.summary: John Liu has pioneered a remarkable project that utilizes agricultural byproducts like corn stalks and wheat straw to innovate lithium recovery methods. His technique leverages plant-based scaffolds to effectively concentrate lithium from dilute brines. Through his groundbreaking work, Liu garnered accolades at both state and international science fairs, showcasing a sustainable pathway for reclaiming essential battery materials and underscoring the role of agricultural waste in advancing environmental engineering solutions.

stories.title: Texas teen builds $25 robot sensor nearly 20 times cheaper than existing options
A family bought 11 farms and turned them into a big five wildlife haven
stories.summary: A South African couple began restoring the Great Karoo in 1997 by bringing together 11 former livestock farms into a 67,000-acre reserve. After removing fences, clearing invasive plants and allowing the land to recover, they began reintroducing wildlife. Cheetahs returned after 130 years, followed by rhinos, elephants and lions, while leopards later returned naturally.

‘Impressed by their energy & ambition’: PM Modi meets India’s space startups on National Space Day
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi met with India's space startups, praising their ambition and energy. National Space Day celebrates Chandrayaan-3's successful landing on the Moon's south pole. This achievement marks India's significant progress in space exploration and scientific innovation. ISRO Chairman Narayanan recalled humble beginnings and highlighted global data sharing. The day aims to inspire greater interest in science and technology for all.

stories.title: DMK-BJP secret pact? Vaiko revives allegation as parties spar over delimitation
stories.summary: Vaiko alleges secret preparations for a DMK and BJP agreement in Tamil Nadu. He praised the current Tamil Nadu government for its achievements in its first hundred days. The DMK questioned Chief Minister Vijay's stance on delimitation after meeting Amit Shah. Southern states agreed to resolve water issues through mutual dialogue and constructive solutions. This political exchange occurred during the Southern Zonal Council meeting.

Virginia Beach turned 640,000 tons of garbage into a 60-foot hill, now a 165-acre park
stories.summary: Mount Trashmore Park in Virginia Beach serves as a unique example of transformation, evolving from a large landfill into a vibrant 165-acre recreational area. Opening its gates in 1973, this park now boasts serene lakes, extensive trails, and playgrounds, showcasing innovative landfill reclamation practices. Its picturesque setting attracts visitors who appreciate the blend of nature and community space, highlighting the benefits of repurposing land.

stories.title: Anti-reservation protests: Chirag Paswan says govt will engage if demands presented systematically
stories.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan has signaled that the government plans to engage with the anti-reservation protesters who have rallied at Jantar Mantar. These protesters are advocating for an economic basis for reservations rather than a caste-based system. Paswan noted the existing 10 percent reservation for economically weaker sections and criticized the Congress for their protests outside a police station. Tejashwi Yadav’s backing of students' protests aligns with his political stance.

stories.summary: Chief Justice Surya Kant proposed 'Nyaya Setu' for the BRICS+ bloc. This initiative aims for seamless exchange of highest court judgments among member nations. A judicial fellowship will allow young judges to learn best practices from partner countries. This shared jurisprudence repository will connect eleven legal traditions for mutual benefit. The proposal emphasizes building bridges of trust and fostering economic growth through justice.

‘Could result in injury or death’: Thanedar urges halting ICE’s electric shock glove plan
stories.summary: Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar and colleagues oppose ICE's electric shock glove plan. They warn of potential misuse and severe injury or death from these devices. Lawmakers cite ICE's past record and insufficient training for officers. The proposed procurement involves millions of dollars for thousands of gloves. They implore the Homeland Security Secretary to immediately stop this purchase.

Medical device makers flag new sterilisation labelling rule
stories.summary: New government rules require medical device firms to print outsourced sterilisation licence numbers. This change, effective six months after August 14, 2026, faces industry opposition. Manufacturers fear increased compliance burdens and potential export delays. The Association of Indian Medical Device Industry seeks reconsideration of this new labelling requirement. They emphasize ensuring patient safety without hindering export competitiveness.

stories.title: Cold medicines for under-4s face curbs over safety concerns
stories.summary: The Centre has restricted combination cold medicines for young children. Fixed-dose combinations of chlorpheniramine maleate and phenylephrine hydrochloride are now banned. These combinations pose risks and safer alternatives are available for children. Manufacturers must now prominently display warnings on all affected drug labels. This regulatory action follows extensive reviews and recommendations from expert committees.

stories.title: No work, no study, no training: 8.7 crore Indian youth caught in a career gap
stories.summary: With over eight crore Indian youth facing unemployment, a lack of vital skills hampers their job prospects. Financial barriers restrict many students from accessing crucial paid training programs, while graduates frequently settle for low-paying positions to assist their families financially. There is a stark career mismatch, as only a fraction of graduates find appropriate roles, making subsidized training and earn-as-you-learn opportunities essential for career advancement.

Driscoll's exit could leave the Army without a Senate-confirmed leader. The Army also currently lacks a Senate-confirmed chief of staff. These developments signal significant changes at the Pentagon's senior levels.

This US island was set to become a resort until 2 storms changed everything
stories.summary: Assateague Island was once planned as a major resort community with thousands of homes, roads and commercial areas. Two powerful storms changed that future. A 1933 hurricane split the island, while the 1962 Ash Wednesday storm destroyed roads and structures. The island was later protected as a National Seashore in 1965, preserving its beaches, wildlife and natural coastal habitats.

stories.title: 'You don't belong to anyone else, but yourself': Rahul Gandhi's message to young women
stories.summary: During a dynamic gathering in Pune, Rahul Gandhi championed women's independence and personal identity. However, discord erupted between student groups, necessitating police intervention and resulting in multiple arrests. Political factions exchanged blame over allegations of disrupted activities and financial support. The primary focus of the event was to confront significant student challenges, such as job scarcity and examination irregularities, against the backdrop of rising political tension related to youth agendas.

Why Rockefeller secretly bought 35,000 acres, then donated them
stories.summary: In 1927, John D. Rockefeller Jr. quietly began buying large areas of land in Wyoming’s Jackson Hole through the Snake River Land Company. The company concealed Rockefeller’s involvement and eventually acquired more than 35,000 acres for $1.4 million. The land was later donated to the US government and became part of Grand Teton National Park.

stories.title: A Swedish hospital stores winter snow and pumps its meltwater through the building in summer
stories.summary: A hospital in Sundsvall, central Sweden, used an unusual cooling system that stored winter snow for use during summer. The snow was kept in a large, insulated storage area and its meltwater was circulated through the hospital to provide cooling. Researchers found that insulation was essential, as unprotected snow would melt by mid-June. The study showed that stored snow could meet the hospital's cooling demand from May to August.

14-year-old tested whether AI can recognise stress; a basic model beat ChatGPT-4o
stories.summary: Fourteen-year-old Zeynep Demirbas tested four AI models on 3,553 Reddit posts to see how accurately they could detect stress. MentalBERT performed best at about 82%, while ChatGPT-4o scored about 74%. Her findings suggest general-purpose LLMs may not be reliable enough for mental health assessment.

stories.summary: In a remarkable effort to rejuvenate Delhi's Yamuna floodplain, CISF personnel have embarked on an ambitious forest reclamation project. By planting thousands of trees and vetiver grass near Sarai Kale Khan, they aim to combat land degradation and curb soil erosion along the riverbank. This initiative, inspired by a successful ecological effort in Dhanbad's mining regions, is part of a larger strategy for restoring and preserving the Yamuna floodplain.

stories.title: No more boarding pass stamps: New immigration rule for international flyers from Sept 1
stories.summary: International travelers will soon need e-boarding passes on smartphones for immigration clearance. Physical boarding passes will no longer be stamped by immigration authorities from September one. This change aims to streamline the process and reduce passenger inconvenience. A pilot project is also underway to eliminate immigration stamping for Indian passport holders. The Bureau of Immigration is implementing these modernization efforts across airports.

stories.summary: In an innovative environmental initiative, a Boeing 737 from Canadian Airlines has been transformed into an artificial reef off the coast of Chemainus, British Columbia. Sunk in 2006, this aircraft has undergone a thorough cleaning by dedicated volunteers before its descent. Now known as Xihwu Reef, it has become a thriving ecosystem, supporting over a hundred different marine species that benefit from the habitat provided by this repurposed aircraft.

stories.title: 'Sometimes dynastic politics has its benefits': Akhilesh on how 5 family MPs helped SP
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav pointed to the presence of multiple members of his family in the SP and suggested that this had helped prevent a split in the party. "Have you ever wondered why the entire party did not split? Because there are five MPs from the same family. We also have several Muslim MPs, and some staunch socialists, so our numbers would not decrease," he said.

In 2021, 20 bonnethead sharks showed they use Earth's magnetic field to navigate
stories.summary: Bonnethead sharks have shown remarkable skills in using Earth's magnetic field for navigation. In controlled laboratory experiments, these young sharks were tested by manipulating magnetic environments. When exposed to southern magnetic fields, they successfully oriented themselves toward their original capture spot. This discovery implies that sharks might use magnetic fields as a navigational tool. Future studies will be essential to unravel how these creatures manage and utilize this magnetic data.

stories.title: Scientists realised 1,200 Starlink satellites could double as a giant scanner for Earth’s atmosphere
stories.summary: Starlink satellites are now helping scientists map Earth's upper atmosphere. Researchers used orbital data from Starlink to estimate thermosphere density. This method creates a two-dimensional map of atmospheric density variations. The findings offer a new way to study this difficult-to-observe region. Commercial satellite data is becoming an unexpected scientific resource.

stories.summary: "I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said. The lawyers demanding his resignation also sought the implementation of an Advocate Protection Act and questioned the proposed increase in registration fees at State Bar Councils.

stories.title: Victorian station used by British royals near Sandringham is on sale for £1.25 million
stories.summary: Wolferton Station, a former royal terminus renowned for its regal service, has been reinvented as a charming family home. For over a hundred years, it welcomed members of the royal family during grand occasions. Following its closure, a dedicated railway employee intervened to prevent its demolition. Now, this unique property is available for purchase at £1.25 million.

stories.title: Texas constable shuts down 3 Flock cameras after county ends contract, tells firm ‘get your garbage’
stories.summary: Following a contract cancellation with Flock Safety cameras, Hood County officials have initiated a refund request and equipment retrieval. A local constable took the initiative to disable and cover the cameras, openly criticizing the issue of warrantless surveillance. This controversy feeds into a broader discussion across the country regarding the clash between enhanced investigatory methods and the preservation of individual privacy rights.

stories.title: Why smaller US cities are emerging as commercial real estate hotspots
stories.summary: South Carolina shows the highest future potential for commercial real estate demand. A new index by the National Association of Realtors tracks economic indicators for this growth. St. George, Utah, leads individual metropolitan markets with strong office employment gains. Smaller and midsized markets demonstrate significant momentum compared to major coastal hubs. This index identifies areas where demand may be building based on data.

'No compromise': BJP passes resolution against Congress on Vande Mataram; vows nationwide protest
stories.summary: The BJP has condemned the Congress party's decision to sing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram. This move is seen by the BJP as undermining the national song's significance and legacy. The party passed a resolution to protect the honor and national character of the complete Vande Mataram. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also attacked the Congress Working Committee's resolution as anti-national.

IndiGo A321neo grounded after tail impact during Gorakhpur landing
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A321neo aircraft experienced a tail impact during its landing approach. The flight from Delhi to Gorakhpur made a successful landing on its third attempt. Scratches were observed around the APU inlet during a post-flight inspection. The aircraft remains grounded at Gorakhpur airport for necessary maintenance. Technical and regulatory clearances are awaited before the plane resumes operations.

BJP plans nationwide 'Seva Pakhwada' from Sept 17 ahead of PM Modi's 25 years in public office
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is set to launch a nationwide 15-day campaign, 'Seva Sankalp Mahotsav', to highlight Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 25-year journey in public life and organise service-oriented programmes across the country.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Socrates: "The difficulty, my friends, is not in avoiding death, but..."
Asia’s high-mountain ‘water tower’ is losing 24 billion tonnes of groundwater annually, new research finds
stories.summary: Groundwater reserves in High Mountain Asia are experiencing severe depletion annually due to a combination of climate impacts and excessive human water usage. The irrigation needs in the lower basins dramatically exacerbate groundwater storage losses. If current consumption trends continue, projections suggest that depletion will persist. Although temporary glacier melt may provide a short reprieve, this will be followed by a more rapid decline.

stories.title: New snake species named after Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash; here’s why scientists chose him
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have unveiled a new non-venomous snake species from New Guinea, named Lielaphis slashi. This remarkable naming pays tribute to Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, also known as Saul Hudson, who has always been captivated by reptiles and the natural world. First encountered during past fieldwork, this small ground-dwelling snake signifies the incredible biodiversity and urgent conservation efforts needed in New Guinea.

stories.title: Logan Paul has listed his 78-acre California ranch with an extraordinary past for sale at $3 million
stories.summary: Logan Paul has put his notorious California ranch on the market for three million dollars. Once the base for Timothy Leary's LSD operation, this secluded 78-acre property boasts an off-grid retreat experience. Acquired by Paul in 2019, the ranch has seen numerous enhancements. Speculation suggests he may now shift his real estate focus to Puerto Rico.

stories.summary: Nestled in Pound Ridge, New York, this extraordinary home is listed for fifteen million dollars. Its mirrored facade seamlessly merges with the lush forest while reflecting the beauty of each season. Crafted by KieranTimberlake, the design emphasizes harmony with nature. Inside, expansive glass walls invite vibrant woodland views, creating a tranquil indoor-outdoor flow. This distinctive residence promises both privacy and proximity to New York City.

Of funds from 19 common donors in 2024, BJP got nearly four times as much as Congress
stories.summary: During FY2024-25, national political parties disclosed over ₹6,600 crore in donations, with the BJP claiming the lion's share at more than ₹6,000 crore. Notably, nineteen donors were recorded on filings for both BJP and Congress, contributing nearly ₹258 crore collectively. This highlights the significant sway that the business and corporate sectors hold over political financing in India.

BJP chief Nitin Nabin holds first meeting with new team ahead of polls

The party unveiled a 65-member team with many new faces appointed. Key positions saw Vasundhara Raje and Ram Madhav named vice presidents. Piyush Goyal returned as treasurer while other roles were also filled.

stories.title: 14 yrs on, NMC still trying to update national register of docs
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission is putting forth a new proposal for mandatory re-registration of doctors across the nation. In the past, efforts to modernize the national registry faced significant challenges. This strategic chemical operation was designed to halt the deterioration of the lake's environment. Following the fish removal, biologists introduced native trout to reinvigorate the food web and support recreational fishing. Enhanced barriers and regulations now safeguard this restored aquatic habitat, exemplifying effective freshwater management.

'Can Standard 6 be spared 3-language plan this year?' asks SC

Ex-SC judge Subhash Reddy to lead probe into action on CJP Parliament march

stories.title: Tasmania spent 28 years removing invasive carp from two lakes; after 49,301 fish were...
stories.summary: After a remarkable 28-year campaign, Tasmania's fisheries service has successfully eliminated invasive common carp from Lake Sorell and Lake Crescent. This effort has seen the removal of over 49,000 harmful fish, leading to clearer waters and the revival of native plant life in marsh areas. The resurgence of wild brown trout has also enhanced recreational fishing opportunities for anglers, proving that large lakes can recover from invasive species.

stories.title: 'I am deeply sorry for the harm caused': Indian-origin hospital CEO takes responsibility for massive drug mix-up at a Nashville hospital during routine surgeries
US ambassador Sergio Gor in Ladakh, may meet Dalai Lama in first trip since Galwan clash
Govt announces panchayat poll process in Ladakh to fill ‘democratic vacuum’, district council polls next
Houses damaged in Jammu village subsidence; families take shelter in tents
First time in 100 years, North American river otter spotted in the Bronx River: 'I could hardly believe what I was seeing'
Both pilots fell asleep as a plane carrying 153 passengers drifted off course
stories.summary: In a startling incident, two Batik Air pilots dozed off simultaneously for roughly thirty minutes, causing their aircraft to veer off course. Communications from air traffic control went unanswered during this time. Thankfully, the plane landed without any injuries, prompting Indonesian authorities to reassess protocols regarding pilot fatigue and procedures for night operations to ensure safety.

stories.title: In 2002, New Mexico began one of America’s largest native-fish restoration projects...
stories.summary: A significant conservation initiative has successfully reinstated native trout species across more than 120 miles of streams by eliminating non-native predators and restoring habitats in two states. The reintroduction of the Rio Grande cutthroat trout has led to the establishment of a self-sustaining population, averting the need for federal endangered species status. This successful strategy serves as a blueprint for other western states aiming to restore native fish populations.

stories.title: Manchester synagogue terror attack: Iraqi national charged over failure to disclose information
Find out who your MP is: Canada's Portage College asks protesting Indian students to approach politicians for work permit woes
In 2006, Idaho launched a bounty-and-netting war on invasive lake trout; a decade later...
stories.summary: A vigorous initiative employing commercial nets and angler incentives has successfully diminished the population of invasive lake trout. This management program has fostered a remarkable resurgence of native species such as rainbow trout and sockeye salmon. Hydroacoustic assessments revealed kokanee densities that haven't been observed since the 1970s. The rebound of kokanee has instigated beneficial shifts throughout the broader ecosystem.

stories.title: 68-year-old Sheila Consaul bought Ohio lighthouse for $71,010 in 2011, restored it for over $300K
stories.summary: At 68, Sheila Consaul owns Ohio’s historic Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse, which she bought for $71,010 at auction in 2011. After years of restoration and more than $300,000 in investment, she transformed the abandoned century-old landmark into an off-grid summer home featuring rainwater collection, solar power, historic interiors and stunning views of Lake Erie.

stories.title: Major UK hotel chain CEO Joanna Boydell resigns amid security failings, sexual assault cases
In 1911, Norwegian whalers released 10 reindeer on South Georgia for food and hunting
stories.summary: In 1911, reindeer were introduced to South Georgia by Norwegian whalers. This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's Hormuz 'total control' claim, says strait will reopen only on Tehran's terms
Six years after Michigan dam disaster, water returns to Smallwood Lake
stories.summary: Smallwood Lake in Michigan has started refilling after work on Smallwood Dam reached substantial completion in July. The refill began on August 4 and is expected to take eight to 10 weeks. Meanwhile, work continues at Secord and Edenville dams, with Secord facing a delay after crews found a problem with a spillway gate.

stories.title: 2.98 lakh URLs sent for takedown; I4C flags scams, CSAM and other unlawful content
stories.summary: Government departments requested removal of nearly 2.98 lakh URLs from social media platforms. States accounted for the majority of these takedown requests, sending 2.44 lakh URLs. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre flagged over 51,000 URLs related to various scams. This action follows widespread student protests and content blocking reports on social media. Government rules were amended to expedite the removal of unlawful online content.

stories.title: Virgin Australia removed a wheelchair user because his mobility device would not fit under his seat
stories.summary: Virgin Australia has issued an apology to Shane Hryhorec after he was removed from a flight due to a misunderstanding regarding the safety of his wheelchair's power add-on motor. Despite Hryhorec's explanation that the device easily detaches, airline staff insisted on his removal. This incident unveils the need for improved accessibility training in airlines. In response, Virgin Australia is reassessing staff procedures and offering Hryhorec a full refund.

stories.title: Parliamentary panel flags critical operational gaps at NGT, suggests measures to improve its efficiency
'Deceived, new fight begins': Jharkhand students after HC stays exam cancellation order
84-year-old woman found alive in rubble three days after Indonesia quake
stories.summary: In an inspiring turn of events, an 84-year-old woman named Paulina Pobi was successfully rescued after enduring three harrowing days trapped under rubble in Nitunglea village on Flores island. Against the odds, she survived without sustenance, while rescue teams faced significant obstacles from landslides and damaged infrastructure. This incredible story of survival emerged as a beacon of hope amid the widespread destruction and displacement caused by the earthquake.

stories.title: 'Must work together': Assam, Meghalaya CMs speak as Shillong violence triggers border tensions
US Waffle House cook's rap praising chain topped 1 mn TikTok views; weeks later, he was fired
stories.summary: Edric Riley, known as “Rockstar Riley” and the “King of Waffle House”, went viral after his rap song “Waffy Options” praising the restaurant chain crossed 1 million TikTok views. Weeks later, Waffle House fired him, citing repeated violations of its rules on filming promotional content on company property. Riley says he was promoting a company he loved.

stories.title: Help us: 4 Indian-origin teens from New Jersey call 911 during Mount Lafayette hike; they will have to pay a hefty fine for 'unprepared' adventure
Separated by Hamas in Oct 7 attack, Israeli couple reunites to marry 10 months after engagement
Why Pakistan’s donkeys are becoming valuable in China: What is driving this surprising demand
stories.summary: Pakistani donkeys are increasingly valuable due to rising Chinese demand for ejiao. China's own donkey population struggles to meet the demand for this traditional product. Pakistan has become a key part of this international supply chain after finalizing export protocols. The rising prices of donkeys impact local families who depend on them for livelihoods. This situation highlights the complex intersection of local needs and global trade.

stories.title: Delimitation, NEET and Cauvery: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay discussed with Amit Shah
stories.summary: Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah, Vijay, who is also the council's vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states which have successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation. He said the issue had become particularly important as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census nears its end.

stories.title: She got her first dolls' house at 8; now, at 101, she runs a museum
stories.summary: Val Ripley, aged 101, continues her lifelong fascination with dolls' houses and their historical significance. Her childhood toy, lost during the war, was rediscovered and inspired a museum. This museum showcases miniature homes as documents of social history and changing lifestyles. The collection features dolls' houses dating back to 1840, reflecting evolving domestic life. Val's enduring connection to these tiny worlds spans nearly a century.

stories.title: Texas woman left 6 acres in 1916; her governor son added 250 acres to create its first park
stories.summary: Isabella Neff's generous donation of six acres to the Leon River marked the beginning of Texas' first state park. Her son, Pat Neff, significantly augmented this by contributing an additional 250 acres. Developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park faced challenges from flooding, necessitating ongoing repairs. Today, Mother Neff State Park is a shining example of familial generosity and commitment to preservation.

stories.title: Car salesman becomes Belgian prince after DNA test confirms royal paternity

Massachusetts police officer accused of using Flock cameras to track her ex-girlfriend
stories.summary: In a significant move, New Bedford police have paused their automated license plate reader system following allegations of misuse by officer Emily Pacheco. Investigations revealed a troubling number of searches for one specific vehicle's license plate. Pacheco is currently on administrative leave while inquiries continue, alongside an extended abuse prevention order from a judge. This incident raises critical issues regarding surveillance practices and the implications for data privacy.

stories.summary: Chairing the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Tamil Nadu's Mahabalipuram, the Union home minister said: "The people of South India and the governments have also established many excellent traditions in the fields of innovation and revenue generation." He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

Battle for UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi': Why parties are wooing women voters like never before ahead of 2027 polls
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh elections now prioritize women voters, who are a significant electoral force. Women's turnout has consistently surpassed men's in recent polls. Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers. Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters. Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

NASA offers up to $500,000 to develop technology for tracking atmospheric drag
stories.summary: In an effort to enhance the understanding of upper atmospheric conditions, NASA is inviting proposals for affordable technology solutions. The Orbital Clarity Challenge aims to refine predictions regarding satellite orbit variations caused by atmospheric drag. Participants stand to win up to $500,000 for their innovative concepts, along with the opportunity for a free test flight to test their technologies.

Built in 1913, this 177-foot steam tug survived two world wars but sank after hitting a...
stories.summary: Amidst severe drought, a historic steam tug once lost beneath the Sava River has resurfaced, delighting locals who flock to witness 'Sava's Titanic'. This vessel, which sank in 1945 after a tragic encounter with a mine, revitalizes memories of the Balkans' complex history. Its emergence underscores the grim water shortages plaguing significant European rivers today.

stories.title: America’s favourite vegetable could be hit by California drought: Over 90% of fresh broccoli comes from the state
stories.summary: The ongoing drought in California threatens the broccoli supply of the entire nation. Estimates indicate that shipment reductions could exceed twenty percent if conditions worsen. Experts propose that by growing more broccoli on the East Coast, costs related to supply chains could decrease and food miles reduced, leading to a more robust and dependable broccoli market across the country.

'UGC regulation under reconsideration', govt tells SC on controversial equity rules
stories.summary: The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the top court on January 29. At the time, the court said the provisions were "prima facie vague" and could have "very sweeping consequences", warning that they could potentially divide society and have a "dangerous impact". The court had also asked the Centre and the UGC to respond to three petitions challenging the new framework.

stories.title: Brazilian mother and daughter create seven-bedroom home from more than 8,000 glass bottles
stories.summary: A visionary mother and daughter duo transformed sustainability into an art form, building a seven-room home out of more than 8,000 recycled glass bottles. Incorporating elements like reclaimed wood and toothpaste tubes, this remarkable endeavor addresses the dual challenges of beach pollution and housing shortages in Brazil. Named the Salt House, it stands as a sustainable residence and an inspiring venue for community education on environmental responsibility and innovative reuse.

For over 50 years, Elizabeth Dickens recorded Block Island's birds, creating a historic record
stories.summary: For more than five decades, Elizabeth Dickens kept a detailed account of bird sightings on Block Island. Her comprehensive journals offered insights into local bird populations and their migratory habits while she inspired students through educational efforts about avian life. Dickens' commitment to her craft resulted in invaluable contributions to ornithology, emphasizing how crucial careful observation is for comprehending the natural world.

Germany opened a solar-walled city hall in 2017 that produced surplus energy
stories.summary: The newly constructed city hall in Freiburg exemplifies sustainability, generating excess energy through high-performance solar panels embedded in its roof and walls. Equipped with top-tier insulation and a heat recovery ventilation system, the facility efficiently optimises energy use. It also leverages groundwater for temperature control. Serving as a model for public sector energy initiatives, this striking structure highlights the potential of green technology in urban settings.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Carl Linnaeus: "Human beings, having, above..."
stories.summary: Human reasoning provides us with a special lens through which we can observe and understand nature. This ability to study and reflect upon natural processes imposes an ethical responsibility on us to avoid exploiting the environment. By grasping the intricate connections within ecosystems, we appreciate our place in the natural world. The wisdom of Linnaeus serves as a guiding light for today's pressing ecological issues.

'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul Gandhi attacks Sangh over ideology
stories.summary: Speaking at the "Hara Bhara Swaraj: A Tribute to Rajiv Gandhi's Vision" programme, the Gandhi Scion described the ideological contest in India as a deeper struggle over how people understand themselves, freedom and their place in society. The Congress leader also drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj', saying no organisation or individual could claim to know what is true for another person.

stories.title: Australian farmer spent three decades restoring land he once cleared; 24 bird species now live there
stories.summary: About three decades ago, King Island farmer Fred Perry began changing the way he managed his land after his children urged him to protect the environment. Once known for clearing native vegetation, Perry and his wife Shona began fencing and replanting parts of their farm. The long-running effort has restored habitat and brought 24 bird species to the property year-round.

EDP445 in trouble as Kern County DA re-examines 2021 "cupcake" incident after new documentary
stories.summary: EDP445 is facing renewed scrutiny after the Kern County District Attorney’s Office reportedly re-examined his 2021 “cupcake” incident following statements featured in Mike Clum’s documentary. The sheriff’s office says it is not actively investigating unless new information emerges. An extended documentary clip also shows Moreland discussing Jeffrey Epstein, Jared Fogle, R Kelly and Michael Jackson.

As 30% of Japan's temples risk disappearance by 2040, monks are using AI to help people speak with Buddha
stories.summary: By 2040, Japanese temples may face closure due to dwindling religious commitment among the populace. In a bid to attract more visitors spiritually, monks are embracing artificial intelligence to improve operational efficiency and enhance communication with worshippers. While some view AI as a useful guide in matters of faith, others argue that the essential human connection is irreplaceable.

stories.title: Doctors gave Seattle shipbuilder months to live; he sold his business, moved to an island and lived another 38 years
stories.summary: Robert Moran, Seattle's former mayor, made a monumental gift of thousands of acres for a state park. Following a serious illness, he relocated to Orcas Island, where he developed picturesque forest lands into a personal estate. His visionary donation led to the establishment of Washington's first state park, named Moran State Park in his honor, which remains a beloved destination to this day.

stories.title: 18-year-old Texas student trains da Vinci robot to remove tumours; succeeds in 3 of 4 tests
stories.summary: A brilliant eighteen-year-old student has engineered a cutting-edge framework designed for surgical robots. Utilizing a simulation strategy, this innovative system instructs robots on autonomous tumor excision. Tested on a da Vinci surgical platform alongside gel models, it achieved success by removing tumors in three out of four trials. This pioneering research paves the way for the future of medical robotics.

stories.title: Manhattan’s traffic-packed Broadway is slowly becoming a 5-mile wildlife corridor
stories.summary: Manhattan’s Broadway medians are being replanted with native Northeast species under a long-term project by the Broadway Mall Association. The Great Green Way covers five miles of Broadway and aims to connect 83 green malls into a corridor that can support birds, bees and other wildlife. Twelve malls have been restored so far, with more planting planned through 2026.
