In 1970s, Marty Bluewater bought land on island planned for 800 homes; he is now its only resident
stories.summary: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.

US Air Force major held again days after arrest for calling for Trump’s impeachment
stories.summary: A US Air Force major, Jason Watson, finds himself detained once more for voicing his criticism of President Trump and advocating for his impeachment. Currently in pretrial confinement, Watson's refusal to wear his military uniform led to this latest arrest. This incident follows his earlier detention on the Capitol steps for expressing political opinions, showcasing his awareness of the repercussions he faces for his stance.

stories.title: Panic in Amethi as 29 copper spheres emerge from ground during house construction; Archaeology (ASI) team examines suspected ammunition
stories.summary: During construction work in Bhanauli village, workers discovered twenty-nine large metal spheres buried deep within the ground. These intriguing copper spheres, each measuring sixty centimeters across, resembled ancient munitions. Local police and the Uttar Pradesh Archaeology Department quickly secured the unusual find. Specialists are now engaged in examining the spheres to determine their historical significance and origin, with plans for additional archaeological research to ascertain their context.

stories.summary: In Tamil Nadu, Union Home Minister Amit Shah presided over a pivotal Southern Zonal Council meeting, gathering representatives from five states alongside three Union Territories. The discussions focused on crucial matters such as water sharing and infrastructure advancements. This council acts as a vital forum for fostering dialogue between state governments and the Centre, demonstrating a commitment to cooperative federalism and effective dispute resolution.

Oldest evidence of life on Earth has been discovered in India in a 3.4 billion-year-old layered rock shows signs of microbial life
stories.summary: Recent discoveries in India have unveiled biological traces that date back approximately 3.5 billion years, indicating a significantly ancient origin of life on Earth. Researchers have confirmed the presence of photosynthetic activity and intricate metabolic processes within these samples, which originated from environments close to underwater hydrothermal vents. This remarkable finding represents the oldest known biological materials found in rock formations.

stories.summary: India urged greater transparency in UN Security Council sanctions decisions. Membership must not legitimize terrorists or pursue narrow political interests. Delays in appointing subsidiary body chairs affect Council effectiveness and credibility. Elected members seek more involvement in key UN processes. The Council's structure needs to reflect global changes since 1945.

stories.title: India makes its vow for longevity: Country's first longevity summit concludes at Fairmont Mumbai
Pulitzer Prize-winning poet bought a barren land in Hawaii and turned it into a 19-acre forest with more than 3,000 palms
stories.summary: W.S. Merwin, a celebrated poet, found solace and seclusion in Maui during the 1970s, where he dedicated himself to creating a lush 19-acre palm forest. This extraordinary project transformed a barren piece of land into a thriving ecological haven, showcasing an impressive array of palm species. Today, the Merwin Conservancy diligently safeguards this rich environmental legacy, ensuring it remains a vital part of our natural heritage.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that the Centre set up specialized clinics for captive elephants, ensuring they receive essential periodic health checkups. Additionally, the ruling requires DNA mapping of each captive elephant to combat illegal trade. The court emphasizes the importance of maintaining these animals' welfare, instructing states to complete DNA profiling to thwart unlawful commercial activities and transfers.

stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a four-year-old boy stumbled upon a 16th-century gold pendant while metal detecting alongside his father in Essex. This exquisite relic, weighing just 8.68 grams and thought to contain a religious artifact, has been identified as a treasure trove. Valued at an astounding £2.5 million, this find provides fascinating insights into the religious practices and craftsmanship of the 1500s.

stories.title: Valkyrae Defends Thumbnail Artist: streamer says Uncharted art is not AI; warns on artists’ jobs
stories.summary: Valkyrae has addressed AI allegations surrounding her YouTube thumbnails after viewers accused her latest Uncharted artwork of being AI-generated. She defended her longtime artist, Anko, explaining that he creates her livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his creative process. Valkyrae said she understands why people may suspect AI but stressed, “But it’s not AI.” She also expressed concern about AI threatening artists’ jobs and livelihoods.

Owens Questions SD Card Handling: Video shows Terrell pocket card; chain of custody remains debated
stories.summary: Candace Owens’ newly highlighted footage has reignited scrutiny over an SD card removed from a camera positioned behind Charlie Kirk. Owens questions why the card was allegedly taken so quickly and why the person involved appeared to use his phone rather than collect other cards. She stresses that her interpretation is opinion, while raising questions about the footage’s handling, possible communication and why that recording was prioritized.

stories.summary: Millinocket, Maine, once thrived around Great Northern Paper Company, but the mill’s 2008 closure transformed the community. In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.

Following court directives, Roy presented himself to the investigation officer but chose not to respond to the questions asked by the authorities. The court had previously granted him interim pre-arrest bail, providing some protection amidst this legal turmoil.

82-year-old Tony Fahey builds ‘walking on water’ machine for charity record
stories.summary: At 82, Tony Fahey embarks on a daring 24-hour world record attempt on water using a unique human-powered vessel named the aqua elliptica. This remarkable challenge seeks to generate funds for Make-A-Wish UK, reflecting his commitment to supporting children with serious health conditions. Following a serious accident years ago, Fahey returns to the water to showcase his remarkable endurance and innovative spirit.

stories.summary: A talented high school student has pioneered a cutting-edge bioengineering method for the early detection of pancreatic cancer. By utilizing magnetic beads to isolate tumor-derived particles from blood samples, her clinical trials demonstrated remarkable accuracy. Her extraordinary research has secured her a spot as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition, offering a promising new avenue for timely diagnosis and improved patient survival outcomes.

In 1961, British scientists stopped farming a 4-hectare barley field and left it alone; 60 years later...
stories.summary: A groundbreaking six-decade study reveals that passive rewilding effectively fosters the development of lush native woodlands. Through protective thorny scrub, young trees thrived, shielded from herbivores, while wind and jays ingeniously spread seeds, outlining the woodlands’ unique patterns. After fifty years, the area began to mirror the characteristics of ancient woodlands, showcasing an eco-friendly and budget-friendly approach to achieving woodland restoration objectives.

In 1963, a California builder made a house that rotates 320 degrees using two washing-machine motors
stories.summary: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.

stories.title: Giant 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire after nearly 90 years as scientists explain UK return
stories.summary: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.

stories.title: Florida’s python invasion was followed by a huge drop in native mammals
CCPA fines Amazon Rs 1 lakh for misleading ‘Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad’ listings
At least 100 killed after illegal gold mine collapses in Central African Republic
Man and his dog uncover a 3,400-year-old Bronze Age axe in England
stories.summary: In an English forest, a fortunate man and his dog uncovered an astonishing 3,400-year-old axe head emblematic of Britain's Bronze Age. This remarkable find sheds light on the enduring mysteries of our ancient past, revealing the metalworking capabilities of prehistoric communities. Artifacts like this one remind us that hidden treasures await discovery in even the most familiar settings.

stories.title: Missouri engineer hand-built an underground home into a hillside; 50yrs later, it remains leak-free
stories.summary: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.

stories.title: Indian caregiver fatally stabbed in Israel, elderly couple’s grandson indicted
Uttarakhand HC rejects bail pleas of 3 convicts in Ankita Bhandari murder case
More than 100,000 ancient shipwrecks may be hiding beneath the Baltic Sea
Meet Natalie Muro, 18-year-old Colorado student who used an invasive plant to fight algal blooms
stories.summary: A remarkable eighteen-year-old student has developed an ingenious device aimed at eradicating toxic algal blooms. Utilizing wind-driven waves and invasive plant species, this unique system demonstrated impressive results in field tests, removing nearly all cyanobacteria and trapping decayed cell matter. This groundbreaking solution offers a cost-effective way to restore and revitalize unhealthy freshwater ecosystems.

stories.title: Amit Shah to chair meeting with CMs, top officials of southern states to resolve inter-state issues
stories.summary: In Mahabalipuram, Home Minister Amit Shah will oversee the Southern Zonal Council meeting, where crucial discussions about water sharing and education priorities among states will take place. Following this, he is set to travel to Siliguri to inaugurate new border security projects, and engage with personnel from Sashastra Seema Bal. His visit will wrap up with a comprehensive review meeting on border security.

stories.title: 1958, the US secretly detonated 3 nuclear devices 100–500 km above the South Atlantic
stories.summary: In a clandestine effort, Operation Argus conducted nuclear tests in the stratosphere over the South Atlantic Ocean. These detonations resulted in spectacular artificial auroras and fleeting radiation belts around our planet. The mission’s intent was to shield against Soviet missile threats and radar detection systems. Yet, the swift vanishing of these barriers caused significant communication disturbances, leading to the formulation of international accords banning nuclear experiments in space.

stories.title: Scientists simulate nuclear strike to stop a 160-metre asteroid impact
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, scientists conducted simulations showcasing the potential of nuclear warheads to neutralize hazardous asteroids. These experiments focused on strategies for fragmenting large asteroids prior to their collision with Earth. While this approach holds promise for planetary protection, it is viewed as a last resort, especially for threats detected late. Ongoing research is crucial for insights into fragment dynamics and their long-lasting consequences.

stories.title: 71-year-old woman donated her farm to create America’s arts park
California couple restores 136-acre farm into thriving wildlife habitat
In the 1970s, a New Mexico architect built Earthships from tyres and cans for extreme weather
stories.summary: Michael Reynolds pioneered the Earthship concept, creating innovative homes constructed from repurposed materials that encourage self-sufficiency. These structures harness recycled resources and natural systems for energy and water usage. Earthships serve as a robust solution against infrastructure breakdowns and natural calamities. This approach is now shaping a wider trend in sustainable construction practices, showcasing an off-grid living model.

Vande Mataram, Chhatron ki Goonj & chanda chori: What Congress discussed in key strategy meet

stories.summary: E20 is petrol containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol. The government has promoted higher ethanol blending as a way to reduce crude oil imports, save foreign exchange and improve India's energy security. India also achieved its 20% blending target ahead of the original 2030 deadline. However, the nationwide shift has generated concerns among some vehicle owners, particularly those with older vehicles.

stories.title: 'Terrible': UK PM Burnham after Palestinian refugee dies alongside wife, daughter in swimming tragedy

4,000-year-old painted stone in Indonesia reveals art carried by ancient Austronesian voyagers
stories.summary: A painted stone found on Indonesia's Wetar Island offers ancient insights. This artifact dates back over 4,000 years and shows early artistic traditions. The artwork predates Neolithic pottery, revealing a significant cultural development. Portable symbols likely traveled with Austronesian voyagers across islands. This discovery reshapes our understanding of ancient maritime cultural exchanges.

stories.title: EasyJet to end all flights from key UK airport from January 2027
AI analysed 15,000 bird skeletons spanning 45 million years
Two Mumbai doctors to receive Pakistan’s highest civilian honour for keeping Jinnah’s illness secret
stories.summary: In a remarkable recognition, two Parsi physicians have been nominated posthumously for Pakistan's prestigious civilian award. They upheld the confidentiality surrounding Muhammad Ali Jinnah's terminal health condition prior to Partition, demonstrating a silent commitment to their professional ethics. This discreet dedication played an inadvertent yet significant role in the formation of Pakistan. The award ceremony is scheduled for March 2027.

stories.title: Destroyed by a 2015 storm, a Virginia refuge beach lot is now moving 2.5 miles north
stories.summary: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge is relocating its beach facilities to a more secure northern position following significant storm damage. This proactive approach not only aims to cut future repair costs but also accommodates the natural shifts of the island. While new parking arrangements will be established, the former site will transition back into its native ecosystem.

stories.summary: The proposed initiative, called 'One Day, One University', is aimed at strengthening the government's engagement with young people. During these visits, ministers are expected to hold discussions with students, hear their views on issues affecting the country and explain government schemes meant for students and young people. The plan comes at a time when student protests over the NEET paper leak issue have intensified in parts of the country.

stories.title: At 14, Sheri Lynch got a grey hippo; 40 years later, she had 1,086 items
stories.summary: Sheri Lynch has achieved Guinness World Records fame for her extraordinary hippo collection, which began with a single plush toy gifted to her in her teenage years. Over the span of more than forty years, she has gathered more than a thousand hippo-themed treasures from various corners of the globe.

Bought in 2016, Indiana bishop’s former home with chapel is now listed at $1.28 million
stories.summary: After nine years of dedication, an Indiana family has lovingly restored a historic home that once served as a Catholic bishop's residence, complete with a private chapel. Purchased at auction in 2016, they meticulously preserved its original features and completed extensive renovations. Now listed for $1.284 million, the family is ready to embark on new adventures and explore the world.

stories.title: European wild boars escaped a North Carolina hunting ranch in 1912; a century later...
stories.summary: Invasive European wild boars, originally introduced to the area in 1912, are wreaking havoc within Great Smoky Mountains National Park. To mitigate damage to delicate ecosystems, park management annually removes around 275 of these feral hogs. The boars breed with domestic pigs, creating hybrid species that further disrupt native wildlife. Efforts to control their population involve trapping, shooting, and implementing fencing strategies.

stories.title: Sumit Sarkar: The Citizen Historian
stories.summary: Professor Sumit Sarkar significantly impacted the understanding of Indian nationalism, illuminating its intricacies through comprehensive analysis. He explored the evolution of nationalism, internal disputes, and collective movements, while challenging conventional binaries. His focus on ordinary people's cravings for justice defined his contributions as a public thinker and citizen historian. This article pays tribute to his influential teaching and the lasting academic heritage he leaves behind.

stories.title: FSSAI action prompts Amway, Emami, four other brands to drop '100%' product claims
stories.summary: FSSAI said Bonn Biscuits had used a "100%" claim in an for its Bonn Cummin Flavor Jeera Bite Biscuits, 76 gm. The company has since removed the claim from its website. Emami was also asked to address its use of a 100 per cent claim for Zhandu Honey. According to FSSAI, the company complied with its advisory and took corrective action.

A British duke sent six Himalayan tahr to New Zealand in 1904; five survived the voyage, and...
stories.summary: Himalayan tahr were introduced to New Zealand's South Island by British aristocrats in pursuit of sport hunting back in 1904. Quickly multiplying, these creatures turned into an invasive species, wreaking havoc on native alpine ecosystems. Control measures, including government-led aerial shooting, have not proven entirely effective, creating a challenging situation for conservationists and hunters alike. The management of tahr remains an ongoing struggle within New Zealand's wildlife strategy.

stories.title: Young YouTuber Buys NYC Apartment: Eden Masliah mixes savings and inheritance; questions feeling fully proud
stories.summary: YouTuber Eden Masliah, 21, has purchased a $740,000 two-bedroom N.Y.C. apartment after saving about $250,000 from her content career and using money left by her late father for an investment. Although the purchase marks a major milestone, Masliah admits she struggles to see it as entirely her achievement because of her inheritance. She is now renovating the apartment and hopes to create a timeless space that reflects her personal style.

3 killed, 3 injured after truck gas tank explodes at Delhi CNG station while refuelling
stories.summary: A fire service officer said all six injured people were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment. Further information about the rest three is awaited. Fire service personnel also took precautionary measures at the station and worked to bring the situation under control. The cause of the explosion has not yet been established. An investigation is underway to determine what led to the gas tank bursting.

stories.title: Amidst the AI data centre backlash, a Missouri farmer is inviting developers to buy his land
stories.summary: In Missouri, a farmer has taken the unexpected step of inviting data center developers to bid on his land, despite notable local opposition and recent state restrictions. He believes that data centers could revitalize struggling rural economies by creating jobs and generating tax revenue. The farmer also addresses valid concerns about water use and electricity costs, presenting his offer as an opportunity for growth even when local prospects are dim.

stories.summary: Witch Island, previously inhabited by the infamous Anna Chittenden—referred to as the 'Witch of Wall Street'—has transformed into a wildlife sanctuary. After her brief stay, Jane Sewall took on the responsibility of safeguarding the isle from irresponsible tourists. In 1986, Sewall gifted the island to the Maine Audubon Society, which is now overseen by the Coastal Rivers Conservation Trust.

Assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, leading to a crash involving her vehicle. Ayesha's younger sister was injured in the wreck and is now receiving treatment. Authorities have arrested three suspects believed to be related to the attackers, as investigations continue to uncover the motive behind this shocking incident.

stories.title: Congress may move court if Pune curfew blocks Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ event
stories.summary: Congress may approach courts if Pune administration halts Rahul Gandhi's student convention. The party secured college permission for the August 22 event, facing a fortnight's gathering ban. This ban, imposed for protests and festivals, is seen as targeting the Congress program. Previous attempts to block similar conventions occurred in Dehradun, Allahabad, and Kota. The party believes the BJP is attempting to disrupt its youth outreach efforts.

stories.title: In 1943, Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave Springwood and 33 acres to US; estate had 1,500 acres and 500,000 trees
stories.summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt generously bequeathed his family's Springwood estate to the government, substantially enhancing the property throughout his life. By planting over 500,000 trees, Roosevelt transformed the surrounding landscape. This pivotal donation secured the lasting preservation of this notable presidential site, which became both America’s first presidential library and a cherished national historic landmark.

stories.title: FBI puts Indian national Major Singh on Most Wanted list
Meet Kanav Jain: Scottish student who built a low-cost autonomous aircraft to deliver medicines to remote communities
stories.summary: Kanav Jain, a talented Scottish student, has been awarded the prestigious UK Young Engineer of the Year for creating AeroAid, an innovative low-cost autonomous drone aimed at delivering medical supplies. This versatile VTOL quadplane combines the best features of helicopters and airplanes, making it ideal for reaching remote locations. Jain’s mission is to leverage technology for vital humanitarian assistance, reflecting his commitment as a leader in drone technology workshops.

Between 1969 and 1972, US released a weevil to fight musk thistle; it later attacked native thistles
stories.summary: A biological control initiative aimed at managing invasive thistles integrated a weevil specifically targeting musk thistle. Unfortunately, this insect extended its reach to native plant species, leading to detrimental effects on local thistles, including an endangered variety that experienced a decline in seed production. This situation underscores the critical importance of careful evaluation in invasive species control programs.

stories.title: Disney built Disneyland around a family farm that refused a $90 million offer
stories.summary: For decades, the Fujishige family refused to sell their 58-acre farm in Anaheim, even as Disneyland and surrounding development transformed the area. Disney and other developers made repeated offers for the valuable land, but the family continued growing strawberries and vegetables. After years of pressure and a bitter fight with the city, the family finally agreed to sell in 1998, shortly before Hiroshi Fujishige died. The former farm later became the Toy Story parking lot at Disneyland.

stories.title: A 2,500-year-old sacred well in Italy hid bronze offerings and two human skeletons
stories.summary: Archaeologists found an unusual ritual well at ancient Etruscan city Kainua in Italy. Two bronze statuettes and a rare bronze plate were discovered at the well's bottom. These objects were votive offerings placed during a foundation ritual centuries ago. Two adult human skeletons were also found, marking the structure's ritual closing. The findings offer new insights into Etruscan city foundations and religious traditions.

stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's party placed Mayor Mamdani's image on a billboard. This billboard featured Mamdani alongside leaders hostile to Israel's interests. Netanyahu is campaigning for re-election amid political challenges in Israel. He has increasingly used Mamdani's criticism as campaign messaging. The exchange occurs while Gaza ceasefire efforts remain stalled.

stories.summary: Kandersteg village in Switzerland faces a significant landslide threat from an unstable mountain. Scientists link this danger to thawing permafrost and changing glacier dynamics caused by climate change. While the threat is not immediate, authorities have prepared evacuation plans and monitoring systems. Residents are aware of the risks but remain calm, trusting the implemented safety measures. This situation highlights the increasing natural risks faced by mountain communities globally.

stories.title: Kansas couple builds tornado-resistant home from tyres, cans and boxes
stories.summary: In an innovative twist on sustainable living, a couple in Kansas is transforming discarded items into a unique residence. This Earthship features around 1,000 tires and 16,000 aluminum cans, built to endure severe weather, including tornadoes and fires. It will autonomously generate power, harvest rainwater, and process wastewater, demonstrating how waste can be creatively repurposed into a haven.

stories.title: 'Foolproof system in place, difficult to breach': Centre lists NEET exam security measures before SC
In 1993, an art historian found a forgotten painting; 33 years later, its female creator was rediscovered
stories.summary: A remarkable find by an art historian in 1993 ignited a relentless pursuit to recover the lost masterpieces of Michaelina Wautier. This accomplished 17th-century painter's works had long been misattributed to men throughout history. The pivotal recovery of her 'The Five Senses' series in 2020 heralded a new era, culminating in a landmark exhibition at London's Royal Academy in 2026, finally restoring her rightful legacy after centuries in the shadows.

stories.title: A rotating 'garbage island' spreads over 1.6 million sq km in the Pacific with 50 kilograms of plastic per square kilometre
stories.summary: Between the shores of Hawaii and California floats a staggering 1.6 million square kilometers of plastic debris. This island of waste includes not just nets and ropes but also countless microplastics that pose serious threats to marine wildlife. Animals often mistake plastics for food, while others become trapped in ghost fishing gear.

'Voice sample is not required': Rahul Gandhi’s counsel opposes plea in Savarkar defamation case

Satyaki Savarkar's deposition also brought Godse-RSS links into focus during cross-examination. The defamation case stems from remarks made by Rahul in London during 2023. stories.summary: India's High Commissioner emphasized Prime Minister Modi's desire for a memorable visit. He assured Prime Minister Rahman of an appropriate and honorable reception. Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, for a longer duration. Medical reports indicated fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety for the former prime minister. stories.summary: Angie Nixon secured a surprise Democratic Senate primary victory in Florida. She will now face Republican Ashley Moody in the general election. stories.title: US vs ICC row escalates: Trump administration sanctions international court president, senior lawyer
stories.summary: In a significant escalation against the International Criminal Court (ICC), the United States has imposed sanctions on two prominent officials, including the ICC president and a senior trial lawyer. The streamer last appeared at WrestleMania 42, teaming with Logan Paul and Austin Theory against The Usos and LA Knight. After their defeat, Paul turned on Speed, leading to a dramatic response when Speed drove him through an announce table. His latest tease could potentially set up another WWE storyline or renewed rivalry with Paul.

stories.title: Streamer Confirms She Is Alive: JollyIRL says she’s hurt after bungee jump; fans reflect on stunt risks
stories.summary: JollyIRL sparked widespread concern after her bungee jump livestream in Pattaya, Thailand, suddenly ended following a loud scream. The abrupt cutoff left viewers fearing she may have suffered a serious accident. The Kick streamer later confirmed she was alive and said her arm and neck were hurting, with possible whiplash. Fans expressed relief and discussed the risks of bungee jumping, while fellow streamer Sneako also voiced concern after watching the viral clip.

Owens And Wilson Clash: Misogynistic slur ignites Kirk case debate; fractures conservative media

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has instructed the Union government to look into the baffling case of Capt Ashish Kumar's disappearance. His wife presented a petition with ransom calls and WhatsApp messages hinting at his possible survival. After DNA tests disproved his presumed death following a ship attack, the court is now requesting a status report on the efforts to locate him from the Solicitor General by Monday.

stories.title: Highways may get traffic 'road test' before launch
Trump's voter ID praise follows Gyanesh Kumar - Sergio Gor meet
stories.summary: Recently, US President Donald Trump commended India’s voter ID system after a meeting between Indian election official Gyanesh Kumar and US Ambassador Sergio Gor. Kumar detailed the extensive issuance of photo identity cards and impressive voter turnout in India. He emphasized that the rigorous examination of elections by political parties contributes to high public trust in the electoral process.

Goa moves SC, seeks life imprisonment for Tejpal for sex assault

The state argues that his current penalty is insufficient given the severity of the crime. They emphasize that Tejpal exploited his position of power, suggesting that time should not lessen the consequences for such an offense.

stories.summary: While digging in his San Francisco garden, a gardener stumbled upon an intriguing limestone sculpture. Despite consultations with around fifty experts, its origins remain shrouded in mystery. Testing an air fryer, candle, humidifier, natural gas and incense, he found incense produced the highest average levels, followed by the air fryer. Inspired by concerns about his grandparents’ asthma, Archishman hopes his findings encourage families to improve indoor air quality.

stories.title: Kejriwal attacks BJP after Satyendar Jain's arrest, calls it 'dictatorship'

stories.summary: The Bombay high court (Goa) had recently convicted and sentenced Tejpal to ten years of rigorous imprisonment in the rape case. Tejpal was convicted under Sections 376 (2)(f) (person who is a guardian or in a position of trust or authority rapes a woman), 354-A (sexual harassment) and 354-B (using criminal force on a woman with an intent to disrobe her) of the IPC.

stories.title: NTA removes 600 experts, brings four-tier checks for question papers
AAP leader Satyendar Jain arrested in Delhi Jal Board corruption case
stories.summary: The case includes charges under provisions relating to bribery, criminal breach of trust, cheating and criminal conspiracy. The case was registered on the complaint of Directorate of Vigilance, GNCTD regarding large-scale irregularities, manipulation of tender conditions and criminal conspiracy in the tendering process relating to augmentation/upgradation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) of the Delhi Jal Board (DJB).

stories.title: In 1912, a Black couple bought California beachfront land and built a resort; the city seized it and...
stories.summary: In a remarkable turn of events, the Bruce family has regained ownership of their century-old beachfront property, unjustly seized from them in the past. Following this victory, they have transferred it back to Los Angeles County for approximately $20 million. This land, a cherished destination for African Americans during segregation, will now be utilized for lifeguard training facilities.

stories.title: 'Action will be taken': Maha FDA chief warns SRK, Ajay Devgn, Tiger over Vimal ad notice
In 1885, New Zealand introduced hedgehogs to fight pests; today, they threaten native wildlife
stories.summary: European hedgehogs were brought to New Zealand during the 1800s to help manage garden pests. However, these spiky creatures now pose a grave danger to the country's unique wildlife. They feast on the eggs and young of various native species, significantly impacting fragile ecosystems, particularly those involving ground-nesting birds. As a result, ongoing conservation initiatives are prioritizing hedgehog removal to protect these threatened populations.

stories.title: Russia sent explosives, drone parts to Iran via secret route to rebuild arsenal
'This right here is everything that's wrong with H-1Bs': Trump official knocks on the door of Pakistani event manager Mohammad Abbas accused of selling visas
British Gas customer claimed £300 for solar power but received £38,611.59 by mistake
stories.summary: A British Gas customer experienced an astonishing seven-week ordeal due to a clerical error resulting in a £38,000 overpayment. The lack of clear recovery procedures from customer service compounded the issue. Similarly, another homeowner faced bizarre phantom gas bills lingering for months after the removal of their meter. These situations underscore significant administrative shortcomings within utility firms. After persistent media coverage and follow-ups, both customers received deserved compensation.

stories.title: Who 'killed' Jason Arday? The absurd tragedy of Cambridge's 'youngest black professor'
stories.summary: In every version, Jason Arday the human being disappeared behind Jason Arday the argument” — an examination of who built his myth, benefited from it and vanished when it collapsed.

stories.title: Vijay government to give women employees 365 days maternity leave for third child
stories.summary: Announcing the change in the state assembly during the demand for grants for his department, minister D Sarathkumar said the decision was aimed at strengthening the state's focus on social welfare and women's empowerment. The state had gradually increased maternity leave for its women employees over the years. The original 90-day provision was increased to six months in 2011, followed by an increase to nine months in 2016.

stories.title: In 1934, an Arizona couple’s unusual home came with snakes and scorpions
Florida teen Ishanvi Sabniveesu builds AI cane that describes surroundings, works offline and calls for help
stories.summary: Ishanvi Sabniveesu is the innovative mind behind CareCane, an AI-powered cane designed specifically for visually impaired individuals. This remarkable device not only helps users navigate obstacles but also enhances their environmental perception. With offline functionality for broader use and emergency assistance features, CareCane has garnered Sabniveesu second place at the prestigious Invention Convention U.S. Nationals. She is currently focused on introducing additional features and pursuing patent approval.

stories.title: 'Credibility well established globally': MEA on Trump's praise for CEC Gyanesh Kumar
In 1919, German crews sank 52 warships at Scotland's Scapa Flow; decades later...
stories.summary: Following their scuttling in 1919, fifty-two German warships found their final resting place in Scapa Flow. Remarkably, the steel salvaged from these wrecks has been pivotal in numerous modern scientific innovations. This unique pre-nuclear steel has been instrumental in constructing sensitive radiation detectors that safeguard medical imaging and deep-space probes from erroneous readings. To this day, seven of these historic vessels remain preserved for their heritage.

stories.title: Fog Nets Supply Freshwater: Moroccan project turns mountain fog into piped water
One dead, over 200 ill in UK Salmonella outbreak: Symptoms, cause and all you need to know
Indian students' protest in Canada: Cops identify 12 individuals who have no legal status and could be deported
Army chief Seth meets Nepal PM Shah, discusses defence ties amid border tensions
In 1960s, US began displacing around 600 families for a 40-mile reservoir; in 1975 the dam was...
stories.summary: The ambitious dam project planned for the Delaware River faced substantial backlash, resulting in its cancellation. This pivotal decision ultimately fostered the establishment of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, a refuge for the river's unspoiled segments. Factors such as environmental concerns and increasing financial burdens were significant in the cancellation, signaling a major milestone in US conservation efforts and land protection strategies.

stories.title: ‘Don’t lie to children’: Rahul slams Rijiju over his 'no one harmed' during CJP stir remark
‘PM CARES? Hardly’: Congress jabs govt for utilising only 0.01% of relief fund
stories.summary: Domestic donations to the PM CARES Fund fell by 30 per cent to nearly Rs 479 crore in the financial year 2024-25, while foreign donations declined by 18 per cent to Rs 92.8 lakh, according to the fund's latest audit report. The total balance in the PM CARES Fund stood at Rs 8,452 crore as on March 31, 2025, compared with Rs 7,173 crore a year earlier.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Pak SC directs govt to shift Imran to hospital; blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children, and more
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered the government to move Imran Khan to a hospital for his health. The Supreme Court rejected pleas to replace hanging as the death penalty method. Bihar transferred seventeen senior IPS officers amid controversy over police actions. A hand grenade explosion near a Kabul school injured approximately fifty children. Rishabh Pant became the first Indian to hit one hundred Test sixes.

stories.title: Alaska's live bearcam becomes summer hit as brown bears gather at Brooks Falls to catch salmon
stories.summary: A livestream of brown bears catching sockeye salmon at Brooks Falls in Alaska has attracted 7.3 million views this summer, 70% more than last year. The cameras have built a dedicated fanbase that follows individual bears and tracks their feeding habits. The surge comes as large groups of bears gather at the falls, ahead of Katmai National Park’s annual Fat Bear Week.

stories.title: In 1980, Miles Boekeloo sold his 365-acre retreat, keeping 5 acres and its cabin for 25 years
stories.summary: Miles Boekeloo sold his 365-acre Michigan property to the National Park Service in 1980. His family retained use of five acres and their cabin for 25 years. This allowed them to enjoy their retreat while the land became protected. The property, now Boekelodge, is part of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore. The cabin and pond remain as traces of the family's connection.

stories.title: Ritabrata Banerjee to remain Bengal LoP till decision on plea within 2 months, says HC
stories.summary: The bench of Justices Shampa Sarkar and Ajay Kumar Gupta directed that the challenge to his appointment be decided by a single judge within two months. The case was filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, a TMC MLA from the Mamata Banerjee camp, who had challenged assembly speaker Rathindra Bose's decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition.

stories.title: MGNREGA out, VB-G RAM G in: What changes for rural jobs, workers and states
stories.summary: MGNREGA has been replaced by VB-G RAM G, increasing guaranteed employment days. The new scheme features a revised funding structure and allocation framework for rural India. States will now share program costs with the Centre in a 60:40 ratio. This transition aims to create durable assets and link wage work with village infrastructure. Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are projected to be significant beneficiaries of this new program.

stories.title: ‘Gandhi, Nehru, Patel sang the same Vande Mataram’: Kharge hits back at BJP amid row
stories.summary: The BJP had criticised the Congress after a video from the party headquarters showed Kharge and Sonia Gandhi speaking while Vande Mataram was being performed during the August 15 Independence Day programme. The BJP accused Congress leadership of disrespecting the national song and sought an apology. The issue remained part of the political discourse in Goa as two stanzas of Vande Mataram were sung in the event attended by Kharge.

stories.title: A New Jersey couple's 185-acres of land which later turned into a wildlife refuge
British couple on honeymoon die in helicopter crash on Greek island; pilot also killed
Brahmin vote up for grabs in 2027? How Akhilesh is manoeuvring his 'PDA' politics to change UP's caste calculus
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav is strategically extending his political outreach to Brahmins in preparation for the 2027 elections. He asserts that this community has suffered greatly under the current regime. This initiative seeks to enlarge his political coalition, moving beyond his usual support base. Mayawati rebuts this tactic, labeling it as political trickery. The Brahmin vote is crucial, drawing attention from various political factions.

stories.title: Who was Sonia Bellina? French TikToker‘s burned body found in Saint-Gilles vineyard
stories.summary: French TikToker Sonia Bellina's burned body was recently discovered in a Saint-Gilles vineyard on August 12, 2026. DNA testing reportedly confirmed her identity as French authorities opened an assassination investigation. Investigators are examining the scene and searching for evidence, while unverified online claims about a possible meeting before her disappearance continue circulating. No suspect has been publicly identified in the case so far.

stories.title: Scientists tested two Argentine ant baits; one sent them roaming, other drove them near water
stories.summary: The study from the University of California, Riverside, found that two common ant-bait insecticides can cause very different changes in Argentine ant behaviour before the ants die. Thiamethoxam made affected ants unusually active and sent them roaming outside the nest, while boric acid caused ants to stop foraging and gather inside. The findings show that unusual ant activity after treatment does not necessarily mean the pesticide has failed.

stories.title: Indian-origin mom's $1.7 billion school transportation startup is transforming the lives of American students
stories.summary: Ritu Narayan established Zum to address the challenges parents face in student transportation. The company leverages technology to enhance the school bus experience for children. Zum has now achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion dollars and is expanding into the energy market by introducing electric buses. This revolutionary approach is reshaping the way students commute to and from school.

stories.title: Why cops wore civil clothes during Jantar Mantar protest? Delhi Police explains in SC
Bihar transfers 17 IPS officers amid row over AK-47 use during student protests
Ex-BlackRock employee bought 10,000 socks for $100,000; startup hit $2M
Kick streamer JollyIRL's bungee jump incident in Thailand explained after stream cuts mid-jump
stories.summary: Kick streamer JollyIRL worried viewers after her bungee jump in Pattaya, Thailand, ended with her livestream suddenly cutting off. Fans had no immediate update and some feared she may have been seriously hurt. Sneako also reacted with concern. JollyIRL later confirmed she was okay, while saying her arm and neck hurt and that she believed she had suffered whiplash after the jump.

stories.title: PM CARES Fund data made public; balance rises to Rs 8,452 crore
Canadian mom gets a keyboard tattooed on her arm so her autistic son can ‘talk’
Henrietta Lacks died at 31, but her cells lived on and transformed modern medicine
stories.summary: Henrietta Lacks' cervical cancer cells became immortal, revolutionizing biomedical research and medical advancements. These HeLa cells were vital for developing the polio vaccine and studying various diseases. Her family remained unaware of this scientific breakthrough for decades after her death. The story highlights critical ethical debates concerning patient consent and financial benefits. This legacy continues to shape discussions on scientific progress and human dignity.

US mother sues Portland Public School after being barred from campus following gender policy dispute

In 1999, a Texas couple bought 828 acres and protected 817 for whooping cranes
stories.summary: In Texas, a couple stumbled upon endangered whooping cranes residing on their recently acquired land. Committed to their conservation, they dedicated 817 acres primarily for the cranes' winter haven. The Johnsons' property has transformed into a crucial sanctuary for these magnificent birds, demonstrating the essential role that private lands play in the survival of endangered wildlife.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Kate Middleton: "It is lonely at times and you do feel quite isolated. But actually…"
xQc calls out Hasan for blaming "coordinated smear campaigns" over dog controversy
stories.summary: xQc challenged Hasan Piker to take responsibility for shocking his dog rather than attributing it to smear campaigns. He argued that a simple acknowledgment and apology could have effectively resolved the controversy. Moreover, xQc expressed skepticism about Hasan's choice to hire a dog walker, raising questions about his commitment to his pet's welfare. This debate erupted once again following a viral clip featuring Hasan and his dog, Kaya.

stories.title: In 1989, Apple buried about 2,700 Lisa computers in a landfill; here's why
stories.summary: In 1989, Apple buried about 2,700 unsold Lisa computers at a landfill in Logan, Utah, ending the story of one of its biggest early failures. Launched in 1983 with a graphical interface and mouse, the Lisa was ahead of its time but struggled because of its nearly $10,000 price and hardware problems. A computer reseller later tried to upgrade and sell thousands of the machines, but the effort ultimately failed. Today, surviving Lisa computers are valuable pieces of Apple history.

stories.title: California woman donates $1 million to teachers after learning they were underpaid
Bangladesh does not want Teesta dispute to hurt ties with India, says minister Shahiduddin
stories.summary: The Teesta begins in the Himalayas and flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh. It eventually joins the Jamuna, which is the Bangladeshi name for the Brahmaputra. The river is particularly important to northern Bangladesh, where farmers depend on its water. It is also important to West Bengal for irrigation and power generation, with several districts in North Bengal relying on its waters.

stories.title: Ex-Cambridge scholar Nathan Cofnas says he could be murdered after Arday vigil in London
At 75, Jeanne Socrates was badly injured; two years later, she sailed solo around the world at 77
stories.summary: At the inspiring age of 77, British sailor Jeanne Socrates completed a solo, non-stop circumnavigation of the globe. Starting her journey aboard the yacht Nereida from Victoria, Canada, in 2018, she faced tumultuous seas for 320 days. Socrates bravely overcame significant challenges, including repairs and injuries from a serious fall sustained earlier.

stories.title: 'Got trapped in crowd': Bihar govt defends constable who fired AK-47 during students' protests
In 1867, Canterbury released 40 house sparrows to eat pests; 15 years later, they were poisoned
stories.summary: New Zealand introduced house sparrows in 1867 hoping they would help farmers control crop-eating insects. The birds multiplied quickly and soon became a problem, feeding on grains and fruit and damaging wheat, barley and maize crops. Their rapid rise led to organised efforts to control them, including poisoned grain, shooting and bounties for eggs and heads. The story was part of a wider push to introduce European birds for farming and sentimental reasons.

stories.title: 'Tell us our crime': JSSC-CGL exam cancellation ends one protest, sparks another as 2,000 fear job loss
stories.summary: Successful JSSC-CGL candidates protested the Jharkhand government's decision to cancel recruitment exams. They fear losing their government jobs after the cancellation announcement on Monday night. Protesters demanded a CBI probe and an opportunity to defend themselves against allegations. The government defended the cancellation to restore confidence in the recruitment system. Fresh vacancies will provide opportunities for deserving candidates after reforms.

stories.title: Post left Mar-a-Lago to govt hoping it would become 'Winter White House', Trump made her wish true
stories.summary: Mar-a-Lago has a long history that predates Donald Trump and the FBI search. Built in the 1920s by wealthy heiress Marjorie Merriweather Post, the Florida mansion hosted royals, diplomats, lavish parties and charity events. Post later left the estate to the US government as a presidential retreat, but it was eventually bought by Trump in 1985.

‘No state should interfere’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar warns Tamil Nadu over Chamarajanagar killings
stories.summary: Karnataka deputy chief minister warned Tamil Nadu politicians against interference. He asserted Karnataka would protect its territorial sanctity and administration. Tamil Nadu leaders demanded a high-level probe into the August 15 firing incident. Karnataka officials stated forest personnel returned fire in self-defense. The state has ordered a magisterial inquiry and offered interim relief.

stories.title: Indian-origin teen built anti-cyberbullying tech in 2013; now runs non-profit rewarded by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
stories.summary: Trisha Prabhu created ReThink, a mobile keyboard preventing cyberbullying by prompting users to reconsider offensive messages. This initiative grew into a global non-profit organization supporting millions of students worldwide. Prabhu's work earned her significant recognition and substantial funding for her impactful efforts. She continues to lead ReThink Citizens, promoting digital wellness and a kinder internet. Her dedication exemplifies how one motivated individual can drive significant positive social change.

stories.title: Women were barred from Liechtenstein’s throne for 400 years; new rule lets the firstborn inherit regardless of gender
stories.summary: Liechtenstein has made a progressive move by updating its royal succession laws to favor gender equality. Now, the first-born child will inherit the throne, breaking traditional norms. This decision aligns with several European countries where female heirs are already established, like Great Britain, which pioneered similar reforms in 2011. Meanwhile, Japan still grapples with its frustrating male-only inheritance policy that raises many questions.

stories.title: 'No safe harbour if law violated; message has gone home': Government sources on talks with Meta
stories.summary: India has warned Meta that safe-harbour protection is not guaranteed if laws are violated. Discussions focused on content moderation and child sexual abuse material handling. The government seeks greater local sensitivity in content moderation decisions. Deepfakes and synthetically generated content require clear labeling for users. WhatsApp usernames are also being examined across all messaging platforms.

stories.title: 'Please take Gyanesh Kumar to America': Congress's jibe at CEC after Trump lauds Indian electoral system
stories.summary: Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera took aim at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's views on US voter identification rules, highlighting a comment made by Donald Trump that praised India's election system. With a hint of sarcasm, Khera proposed sending India’s electronic voting machines and Kumar to the US. This debate highlights ongoing tensions between Congress and the Election Commission, particularly regarding accusations of vote theft during past Lok Sabha elections.

Florida man arrested after throwing dog poop at neighbour over uncleared mess
Black drongos introduced for pest control later threatened Guam’s native birds
stories.summary: In 1935, the introduction of black drongos to Rota aimed to control agricultural pests. This effort led to the birds establishing their populations, eventually spreading to Guam. However, their aggressive behavior towards native bird species has contributed significantly to declines in local avian populations, highlighting the unforeseen consequences of introducing non-native species into ecosystems.

stories.title: 1,090 cybercrimes, Rs 1,071 crore trail: China-linked gang ‘mastermind’ arrested in Assam
BJP appoints state in-charges for poll-bound UP and Punjab day after unveiling ‘Team Nitin Nabin’
Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "If we aren't willing to pay a price for our values, if we aren't willing to…"
A rare orca known as “La Abuela” was found with wounds consistent with shotgun pellets; could threaten an entire Iberian population of fewer than 40 whales
stories.summary: Spain's Environment Ministry is actively investigating a distressing situation involving Toni, an injured Iberian orca. The oldest member of her pod has been discovered with wounds resembling those inflicted by shotgun pellets, as witnessed by marine conservationists documenting several impacts on her dorsal fin. The Iberian orca population is critically endangered and endures significant threats due to human actions and pollution.

stories.title: $186M cleanup transforms Minnesota lake, creates 14-acre fish habitat
5,000-year-old Japanese pot in New York has a flame-like rim
stories.summary: The Kaen doki, an ancient Japanese pot, carries a history that spans millennia. Distinct in its design, featuring a flame-like mouth and cord-marked details, this earthenware piece exemplifies the craftsmanship of Jomon potters. Built from carefully shaped clay coils with pierced openings, this stunning artifact is a glimpse into the artistic achievements of the past and now resides proudly in The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

stories.title: ‘No intention to attack N Korea’: S Korea Prez Lee after Trump reduces US drills
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung advocates for stronger independent defense capabilities. He defended annual civil-defense exercises as purely defensive measures. These drills occur alongside joint US-South Korea military exercises. President Trump previously instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military drills. Seoul plans to continue strengthening its own defense while maintaining its alliance.

stories.title: Florida man set to be executed in state’s 13th execution of 2026
'You’re fake news, be quiet': Trump snaps at reporter over Korea question
'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates
Meet 17-year-old Tiya Aggarwal, who built a smart watering system for 150+ plant species
stories.summary: Canadian high school student Tiya Aggarwal has won the top prize at a British Columbia entrepreneurship competition for Aquora150, a smart irrigation system designed to automatically adjust care for more than 150 plant species. The system uses humidity-capturing technology to hydrate houseplants while reducing water, plastic and glass waste.

stories.title: Search operations launched at multiple J&K locations over movement of ‘suspected persons’
President Donald Trump tells 10-year-old rescued by teen lifeguard he “wouldn’t” have risked his life to save him
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of courage, 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams saved Nathanial Rai, a young boy, from perilous waters at the California beach. Their heroic rescue, which gained significant attention after going viral, caught the eye of President Donald Trump, who invited both to the White House. Williams emphasized his rigorous training and swift action during the rescue, sparking conversations about lifeguards' official recognition as first responders.

stories.title: 'Not a single protester died': Rijiju defends Delhi police response to Jantar Mantar protests
Tropical Storm Lala in Hawaii: Roads collapse, 100 homes swept away, no power, mobile service; 1 dead

Utility & reliability of caste data to be assessed post-census
'What you did was incredible': Trump meets California lifeguard and boy he rescued
US Supreme Court again rejects Trump's bid to overturn $5mn E Jean Carroll verdict
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court again rejected Donald Trump's attempt to overturn a civil verdict. A jury had previously found him liable for sexual abuse and defamation against E. Jean Carroll. This decision leaves a $5 million judgment in place, which Trump has now paid. Another separate $83.3 million verdict against Trump is still pending before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: CEA bats for E10 fuel; not feasibile, say officials
stories.summary: Officials were taken aback by the Chief Economic Adviser's comments regarding the availability of E10 fuel, which could spark a shift towards lower ethanol blends. Nonetheless, the government is not currently considering the introduction of E10 at fuel stations. Logistical challenges and the necessary infrastructure for managing E10 are cited by officials, who also point out that studies indicate E20 fuel does not pose mechanical risks to older vehicles.

stories.title: ‘Has always treated me with great respect’: Trump’s fresh praise for Kim Jong Un
Supreme Court bars CBI, ED from filing report on Rahul Gandhi's assets
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has stopped agencies from filing probe reports on Rahul Gandhi's assets. Agencies were directed by the Allahabad High Court to investigate allegations of illegal wealth. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued the High Court order was unknown to law. The Supreme Court issued notices and requested the High Court to defer its hearing. No reports will be submitted to the High Court until further orders.

stories.title: Ram Madhav, Biplab Deb, Smriti in BJP’s national team
stories.summary: BJP chief Nitin Nabin announced a new team of national office-bearers on Monday. The party brought in experienced individuals and retained some successful office-bearers. Union minister Piyush Goyal returned as treasurer in the reshuffled team. This overhaul includes many new faces and aims for broad representation. The new team will be in place for the upcoming national election.

stories.title: Meta goes to trial this week, which, if it loses, could change Insta & FB forever
stories.summary: Meta has been hit with a major lawsuit regarding child safety and the addictive nature of its platform. Various states are demanding significant financial compensation and operational reforms, arguing that Meta intentionally crafted features to be addictive for young users. Additionally, they allege that the company collects data from children under the age of thirteen without obtaining proper consent.

stories.title: Frame airfare rules by Sept 7, SC tells Centre
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has set a deadline of September 7 for the implementation of new aviation regulations. Following a request from the government, an extension was granted to finalize these rules. Draft regulations were presented to the bench in a confidential manner. On the aforementioned date, the court will evaluate the completed rules to tackle ongoing passenger grievances regarding unpredictable airline ticket pricing.

stories.title: Only talks can resolve issues, hope Bangladesh PM visits India soon: Trivedi
stories.summary: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stressed dialogue for resolving bilateral issues between India and Bangladesh. He expressed hope that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India should occur much sooner. Bangladesh government attached tough conditions for New Delhi prior to the possible bilateral visit. An Indian business delegation began a three-day visit to strengthen economic engagement. Both nations share a dream and acknowledge inherent challenges within democracy.

stories.title: ‘Does Shanti Act put curbs on compensation by courts?’
There can be no obstacle to elephant movement: SC
Centre may roll out free NEET, JEE coaching as early as October 2
Rajnath slams Rahul's choice of words
States need HC nod to drop poll malpractice cases: SC
Identity of 'Dimagi Naxal Party' founder remains a mystery
14 of 28 chief ministers face serious criminal cases, Supreme Court told
stories.summary: Fourteen chief ministers face serious criminal cases, with Telangana's leader having the most. Many legislators across states also have pending criminal charges against them. In Lok Sabha, 170 MPs and Rajya Sabha, 75 members face criminal cases. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of pending criminal cases against legislators. Special courts are requested to expedite trials for these elected officials.

stories.title: Speedy trial a right of victim too, says Supreme Court
Streamer Pool Incident Debate: Sara Saffari confronts Rawdogmoon; $40,000 Rolex sparks X backlash
stories.summary: Sara Saffari confronted Twitch streamer Rawdogmoon after he threw her into a pool at Cinna’s party while she was wearing a reported $40,000 Rolex. She appeared angry and questioned his decision. Another clip showed Saffari asking about an alleged E-date involving Sophie Rain. The videos sparked mixed reactions online, with viewers discussing both incidents and the watch.

'Every voter had valid photo ID': Trump cites Indian election system to make case for 'Save America Act'
Fake govt offices set up, funds siphoned off in Gujarat
Princess Eugenie reveals baby daughter’s name with touching tribute to Queen Elizabeth II
stories.summary: Princess Eugenie has revealed the name of her newborn daughter with a touching tribute to the late Queen Elizabeth II. Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank have named their third child Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank. The royal said the name honours three people they love and admire, while also reflecting their connection to England and Portugal.

stories.title: 2 Air India pilots have failed dope test so far, taken off duty
3,000-year-old inscription naming Masn may help archaeologists identify the lost Egyptian city
stories.summary: A remarkable sandstone lintel inscribed with the titles of Ramesses II was uncovered at Tell Abu Seify. This inscription reveals valuable information about the restoration of a statue of Horus, the Lord of Masn. Such findings bolster the theory that this site may very well be the fabled lost city of Masn, showcasing evolution from a significant religious and military hub to an industrial quarry through recent excavations.

stories.title: ‘I cannot walk, I use two crutches’: 85-year-old Rochford man told to remove £2,200 driveway
stories.summary: An 85-year-old Rochford man is facing the threat of legal action after being ordered to remove a £2,200 block-paved driveway he built on a grass verge outside his home. David Siggins, who uses two crutches and has COPD, says he was given permission to build it but has now been told the land belongs to Rochford Council.

stories.title: Meet Jasper and Emile: Two Brooklyn teenagers built a Gen Z finance newsletter
'Huge victory for Jharkhand': Student leader Mahto ends 16-day hunger strike after Soren govt accepts demands
From 5,921m summit, historic glide to Ladakh roadhead
Indian-origin CEO says he starts checking his emails at 4.30 am; 'If you want to work eight-to five...'
Meet Mohammed Almuntasir: Libyan photographer's video proves "ghost cat" still lives
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking 2017 video, a Libyan photographer captured the elusive sand cats, marking the first sighting of these fascinating creatures in their natural habitat. This revelation sparked an extensive eight-year research collaboration between zoologist Firas Hayder and photographer Mohammed Almuntasir, who combined their expertise and local insights to gather essential data. Their ongoing efforts are instrumental in enhancing our understanding of sand cat populations in Libya.

stories.title: PDP president Mehbooba says she is ‘dimagi Naxal’; NC blames her for Article 370 abrogation
Indian-origin grandmother with Green Card detained by ICE after living in the US for 30 years. Her daughter is an immigration attorney
Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates: "A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice…"

stories.summary: Thirty lions and tigers from Argentina’s shuttered Lujan Zoo have begun a major relocation to wildlife sanctuaries in South Africa and the US. stories.summary: Researchers in Michigan have helped bring the Poweshiek skipperling butterfly back from the brink of extinction after its US wild population fell to just nine in 2022. Through captive breeding, habitat restoration and carefully planned releases, more than 1,300 butterflies were released in 2025. The recovery effort has now expanded to other endangered butterflies, while restored prairie habitats are helping support wider ecosystems.

stories.title: In 1745, the US welcomed mimosa trees for pink flowers; they later spread invasively
stories.summary: Mimosa, introduced to the United States around 1745, quickly became a sought-after ornamental tree. However, it broke free from cultivation, proliferating in disturbed environments throughout the southern and eastern U.S. Its rapid growth and abundance of seeds have turned it into an invasive species, vying with native flora and reshaping ecosystems. Effective management must focus on both current plants and their future offspring to mitigate this ongoing issue.

These ninth and tenth-century vessels show that local cementation techniques were employed. Residues indicate craftspeople produced brass locally rather than importing finished goods. Lead-isotope analysis suggests local raw material sources were utilised. The findings point to wider technological connections with the Islamic world through maritime trade.

A Maine oyster farm is testing a floating conveyor that moves oyster baskets through water and air
stories.summary: Engineers in Maine are developing an innovative solar-powered floating system tailored for oyster farming. This unique platform incorporates a vertical conveyor that efficiently transports oyster baskets from underwater to above, aiming to enhance production while significantly lessening the labor demands on farmers. Additionally, it aids in shaping the oysters and cleaning their shells from unwanted marine growth.

Got a secret you can’t tell anyone? Visit this ‘grave of secrets’
stories.summary: A unique art installation in Brooklyn offers a place for visitors to anonymously share their deepest secrets. French artist Sophie Calle created a marble obelisk where people can deposit written confessions. This project, which began in 2017, will continue until the year 2042. Secrets deposited will be exhumed and cremated in a ceremonial service periodically. The installation provides a moment of catharsis and a chance for reflective unburdening.

San Diego student develops red-light therapy to help heal wounds in space
stories.summary: An 18-year-old San Diego student has been named a finalist in the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search for developing a low-cost red-light treatment to improve wound healing in microgravity. Leanne Fan built a $200 device to simulate microgravity and found that the treatment accelerated tissue regeneration in flatworms by 95.2%. Tests with human cells also showed faster cell movement during wound closure.

stories.title: Inde Navarrette Cast As Rogue: Ex-streamer lands MCU’s new X-Men role; Obsession paved the way
stories.summary: Inde Navarrette’s career has reached a major milestone after she was cast as Rogue in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot. The actress first gained recognition through roles in 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois before earning critical praise for her intense performance in Obsession. Her journey also includes a past as a Twitch and YouTube streamer. Now, Navarrette is stepping onto Marvel’s biggest stage as one of its iconic mutants.
